title: GG01-01: The SUMMIT Study: A real-world, prospective, multi-center study to evaluate the performance of the Optilume® BPH Catheter System in men with symptomatic Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH)
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The Optilume BPH Catheter System (Urotronic, Inc./Laborie Medical Technologies, Plymouth, MN, USA) is an FDA-approved, minimally invasive drug-coated balloon dilation device developed for the treatment of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) secondary to benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). It has demonstrated symptom improvements comparable to other minimally invasive surgical therapies (MISTs). In this study, we evaluated functional and patient-reported outcomes, including maximum urinary flow rate (Qmax), quality of life (QoL), post-void residual volume (PVR), and responses to a validated symptom questionnaire. METHODS: This prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label study was conducted across five Canadian sites to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of the Optilume BPH System in treating LUTS secondary to BPH. Functional and sexual outcomes were assessed in 30 catheter-free patients at baseline, on the day of treatment, and at 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-up visits. RESULTS: Thirty patients were treated for symptomatic BPH using the Optilume BPH system between July 2022 and August 2025. The mean age was 63.1 ± 7.0 years, and the average prostate volume was 45.9 cc (IQR: 33.7–63.1). The mean procedure duration was 23.4 ± 4.3 minutes, with a median of 21.5 minutes (range: 17.0–31.0). Symptom severity, measured by the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), improved markedly from 23.4 ± 5.1 at baseline to 12.2 ± 6.0 at 3 months, 11.0 ± 6.6 at 6 months, and 10.8 ± 7.5 at 12 months. The IPSS quality-of-life score decreased from 4.7 ± 1.3 at baseline to 2.2 ± 1.6 at 6 months and 2.0 ± 1.6 at 12 months. Sexual function outcomes remained stable, with the MSHQ-Function score changing minimally from 8.3 ± 3.8 at baseline to 7.9 ± 4.0 at 12 months (p=0.955), and the MSHQ-Bother score from 1.9 ± 1.7 to 2.2 ± 1.5 (p=0.972). Similarly, the IIEF total score showed no significant difference, from 43.7 ± 21.3 at baseline to 42.0 ± 23.0 at 12 months (p=0.13). Median maximum urinary flow rate (Qmax) improved from 8.7 ± 3.7 ml/s at baseline to 15.5 ± 7.5 ml/s at 6 months and 14.7 ± 6.9 ml/s at 12 months (p=0.003). Post-void residual volume (PVR) decreased from 95.7 ± 79.1 ml at baseline to 60.3 ± 49.0 ml at 6 months and 63.1 ± 41.6 ml at 12 months. PSA levels remained stable from baseline (1.7 ± 1.6 ng/mL) to 12 months (1.7 ± 1.8 ng/mL). The mean postoperative catheterization duration was 2 days. CONCLUSIONS: Throughout the 12-month follow-up period, patients demonstrated significant and sustained improvements in urinary outcomes and validated symptom scores. Sexual function remained stable, indicating that urinary benefits were achieved without compromising sexual health. These results affirm the findings of the prior EVEREST and PINNACLE studies.

title: GG01-02: Effect of a virtual home hospital pathway on length of stay and recurrent presentations in septic stone patients
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Hospital capacity constraints have underscored the importance of safely expediting patient discharge without compromising care. Traditionally, patients with septic stones remain hospitalized until clinical stability is achieved and culture-directed oral antibiotic therapy can be initiated. However, most patients stabilize within 24–48 hours after source control, yet remain admitted for intravenous (IV) antibiotics and monitoring. To address this, a Virtual Home Hospital (VHH) pathway was introduced on December 16, 2024, enabling early discharge with continued physician oversight, remote vital monitoring, laboratory follow-up, and home-based IV antibiotic administration until rationalization was completed. Our primary objective was to assess for length of hospital stay (LOS). Secondary objectives included assessing the safety of the pathway via rates of re-presentation to hospital, re-admission rates, and the number of subsequent unscheduled healthcare interactions after discharge. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 64 patients diagnosed with a septic stone at the University of Alberta Hospital before VHH implementation compared to 18 patients after, of which 15 (83%) were enrolled in the VHH pathway. Collected data included patient demographics, drainage method and laterality, incidence of positive blood cultures, and ICU admission. Statistical analysis was conducted using SPSS software. RESULTS: No significant differences between age or gender were noted. ICU admission occurred in 13% of pre-pathway patients, with none in the VHH group. Positive blood cultures were seen in 45% of pre-pathway patients and 28% of VHH patients (p=0.18). Following implementation, mean LOS was 3.7 days in the pre-pathway group vs. 2.6 days in the VHH group (p=0.17). The mean duration of VHH admission was 14.5 days, with total antibiotic treatment shortened from a mean of 13.3 days in the pre-pathway group to a mean of 10.4 days in the VHH group (p<0.001). No significant differences were observed in pre-and post-pathway groups for emergency or clinic re-presentations prior to definitive stone surgery (p=0.58 and p=0.28, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Preliminary results suggest that a Virtual Home Hospital pathway is a feasible and safe approach for managing septic stone patients who stabilize rapidly after source control. Post implementation of the VHH pathway, there was a significantly shorter duration of antibiotic treatment which may be secondary to closer outpatient follow-up and antibiotic rationalization. Though no significant difference was noted with respect to LOS, this may be a result of the limited sample size of the post implementation group.

title: GG01-03: Evaluation of testes with micro-ultrasound in men with non-obstructive azoospermia
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: There remain significant limitations in prognostication and pre-operative surgical planning for men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA). Micro-ultrasound (microUS) is a high-resolution device that resolves down to 70 microns, permitting the visualization of seminiferous tubules and their contents. The primary objective of this study is to examine imaging differences in testicular seminiferous tubules using microUS in men with NOA versus in those with normal spermatogenesis. A secondary objective will be the correlation between microUS results and findings at microsurgical testicular sperm extraction (microTESE) in men with NOA. METHODS: This study is a prospective multisite Phase 2 trial at Shady Grove Fertility in Washington, and at the University of Alberta in Edmonton. The trial includes≥20 men with azoospermia and investigative findings consistent with a diagnosis of NOA (elevated FSH and small testicular volumes) and≥20 men with normal spermatogenesis (proven fertility). The ExactVu high-resolution microUS is used to systematically scan each testis in a predetermined grid, searching for isolated tubular ectasia. Imaging differences will include both quantitative measures of tubule diameter, density, and echogenicity as well as qualitative descriptions of the imaging features observed. RESULTS: 28 men with NOA have been evaluated with microUS. Seven men have had surgical exploration for sperm, either prior to or after scanning. Of these, 4 men have yielded sperm, and 3 have yielded no sperm. When examining the reflection and attenuation of the microUS images across these scanned men, differences distinguishing testicular areas with sperm from those without sperm have emerged. Applying Downshift and Nakagami Omega distributions, these areas can be visually represented with heatmaps in which blue areas correlate to architecture patterns in those with sperm, while yellow areas correlate to those without sperm ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191268.85865.a2.03#F1)). Imaging characteristics from men with normal spermatogenesis are currently pending. CONCLUSIONS: MicroUS imaging characteristics appears to be able to differentiate testicular tubules with and without sperm. MicroUS may have a future role in surgical planning and may help optimize results of microTESE in real time using point of care imaging during surgery.

title: GG01-04: Expanding Same-Day-Discharge Aquablation BPH Surgery Outcomes in Ambulatory Surgical Centers: Updated Largest Experience Outcomes of 350 Consecutive Cases
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) surgery is increasingly transitioning to outpatient and ambulatory surgical center (ASC) environments. Aquablation, s robotic, waterjet-based, image-guided resection has demonstrated consistent safety and durability. Our group first reported the feasibility of same-day-discharge (SDD) Aquablation in 40 men in 2023\. Herein, we present an updated analysis of the largest, most contemporary cohort of 350 consecutive ASC Aquablation procedures with extended follow-up to 12 months. METHODS: A retrospective review was performed of 350 consecutive men undergoing Aquablation for symptomatic BPH between June 2023 and September 2025 at a single high-volume ASC. Standardized intraoperative and postoperative protocols included general anesthesia, adjunctive focal bipolar hemostasis, 24F Rusch 3-way catheter with 50 cc balloon, and bladder irrigation with 3 L saline. Same-day discharge was targeted for all patients following hemodynamic stability, hematuria control, and pain <4/10 VAS. Functional and uroflow parameters were assessed preoperatively and at 3, 6, and 12 months. RESULTS: Mean age was 67.5 years and mean prostate volume 122 ml (41–320); 62% had median lobes and 54% were in retention. Mean operative time was 64 min, with 3.6 passes and 36 min of adjunct bipolar cautery. SDD was achieved in 97% (338/350), with 1.5% overnight stays for pre-planned travel and 1.5% for transient hematuria. Mean postoperative recovery time was 3.8 h and Foley removal at 5.2 days. Thirty-day complications were minimal: ER visits 2.5%, hematuria requiring irrigation 1.4%, reoperation 0.5%, infection 0.8%, transfusion 0.5%, and transient stress incontinence 0.5%. At 3, 6, and 12 months (n=320, 290, 202), mean IPSS improved from 30.3 to 7.3, 5.3, and 4.6; QOL from 5.3 to 0.7, 0.6, 0.6; and Qmax from 5.0 to 24.2, 26.1, 23.9 ml/s. Mean PVR decreased from 431 ml to 43–46 ml. Mean TRUS prostate volume decreased ~67%, with stable SHIM and MSHQ-Function/Bother scores. Retrograde ejaculation occurred in ~10%. CONCLUSIONS: This largest series to date confirms that SDD Aquablation in an ASC setting is safe, effective, and durable up to 12 months. Symptom and flow improvements mirror hospital-based series, with low complications and preservation of sexual function. | | | --- | | |

title: GG01-05: Global Prostate Research Disparities: A 25-Year Bibliometric Analysis of Authorship Equity and Disease Focus
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1

speakers.organization: Desai Sethi Urology Institute, University of Miami

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Equitable representation in scientific research is essential to ensure worldwide relevance of disease insights and clinical practice. This study analyzed global patterns in prostate research from 2000 to 2025 to evaluate disparities in authorship contribution and research focus across countries stratified by income level. METHODS: We conducted a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed prostate publications on May 27, 2025. Metadata including publication year, journal, language, document type, authors, affiliations, access status, and author keywords were extracted. Affiliations were assigned to World Bank income groups: high-income countries (HIC), upper-middle-income (UMIC), lower-middle-income (LMIC), and low-income (LIC). Publications were categorized as benign or malignant based on title, abstract, and keywords. Authorship inequality was assessed using Lorenz curves and Gini coefficients. Temporal trends were analyzed using the Mann\\x{2013}Kendall test, and associations between income group and disease type using Pearson's chi-square test. RESULTS: A total of 89,406 publications from 160 countries were included. HICs produced 78.8% of total authorship and 78.0% of corresponding authorship, whereas LICs contributed only 0.09% and 0.11%, respectively. International collaborations accounted for 16.6% of publications, yet 87.9% were driven by HIC authors, with LIC involvement only 0.22%. From 2000 to 2024, HIC representation decreased from 96.6% to 66.9%, with significant increases in UMIC and LMIC participation (p<0.001) ( Table 1). Malignant prostate research dominated the literature (79.9%) compared to benign disease (14.2%), with benign research declining over time. Income distribution and disease-type inequality modestly improved, though LIC progress remained minimal ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191268.85865.a2.05#F1)). CONCLUSIONS: Despite an encouraging rise in global participation, HICs continue to dominate prostate research which remains highly focused on malignancy. Strengthening collaboration in LMICs and LICs is critical to advancing equitable global scientific progress. | | | --- | | |

title: GG01-09: The WASHOUT study: early proactive intervention in emergency haematuria reduces length of stay, mortality andreadmissions
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: There are currently no evidence-based guidelines for the management of emergency haematuria. As a result, clinical practice maybe highly variable and dependent on several factors, including anecdotal clinician judgement, clinician experience, hospital-level resource, and patient comorbidities. The WASHOUT study aimed to investigate variations in the management of emergency haematuria and evaluate impact of variation on patient outcomes. METHODS: A prospective, international, multi-centre cohort study was conducted using the British Urology Researchers in Surgical Training(BURST) collaborative model, incorporating patient and public involvement. The primary outcome was length of stay (LoS) measured from the date of admission to the date of discharge in days. Key secondary outcomes included overall mortality, and readmission to hospital after index admission. Patients were followed up for 90 days. Outcomes were analysed using appropriate statistical models adjusted for relevant covariates. Poisson regression models estimated adjusted relative risk of increased LoS and logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted relative risk of mortality and readmission. RESULTS: Data from over 8,500 patients across 382 centres over a 12-month period, were included. An increase in the number of days between admission and definitive management was significantly associated with increasing LoS and an increased risk of readmission, and death (OR 1.02) (p=0.00). _On comparative analysis, patients with >2 days between admission and completion of_ _management had an average LoS increase of 5.6 days, a 2.5% greater probability of_ _death within 90 days, and a 3.1% greater probability of readmission after adjustment_ _for covariates._ Other factors independently associated with prolonged LoS and increased mortality included frailty, sepsis, upper tract obstruction, and the need for intensive care. Mortality was also higher among patients who did not undergo imaging in the emergency department, lacked a definitive diagnosis during admission, or had malignancy as the underlying cause of haematuria. Higher 90-day readmission rates were observed among patients with a history of radiotherapy, those receiving antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy, patients without prior hospital admissions, and those with longer initial hospital stays. CONCLUSIONS: WASHOUT is the first study to evaluate factors influencing outcomes in patients presenting with emergency haematuria. Based on our findings, we propose patients with emergency haematuria should have emergent imaging on admission and intervention within 2 days of admission if the haematuria has not settled by conservative measures within this time frame. There is an urgent need for evidence-based guidelines to standardise and expedite the investigation and management of emergency haematuria, and improve patient outcomes.

title: GG01-10: Comparing Hounsfield Units, Vickers Hardness, and Surgeon-Perceived Fragmentation Susceptibility between Cohorts of Pure Uric Acid and Calcium Oxalate Monohydrate Calculi
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Higher Hounsfield units (HUs) predict higher energy requirements in shockwave lithotripsy; however, it is unclear how HUs relate to mechanical hardness, a variable many believe is an important stress–strain mechanical proxy in the context of laser lithotripsy and percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL). In this study, our team investigated the relationship between HUs and Vickers Hardness (HV), and whether the operator’s perception of fragmentation difficulty during PCNL correlates with true mechanical hardness. METHODS: Fifteen PCNL-derived stones from St. Michael’s Hospital, Toronto, met inclusion criteria as 100% calcium oxalate monohydrate (COM) (n=8) or 100% anhydrous uric acid (UA) (n=7), as determined by Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy. Mixed stones were excluded to remove compositional confounding. Postoperatively, the primary surgeon was asked to provide a global rating of fragment difficulty using the ultrasonic lithotripter from 1 to 10, with 1 being the easiest and 10 being the most difficult to fragment. All stones underwent ultrasonic cleaning, air-drying, resin embedding, and sequential grinding and polishing to 1 µm to expose an internal cross-section. HV measurements were performed using the LECOLM310 microindentation system at 0.5 kgf load for 10s per indentation. HUs were obtained by aggregating pre-operative CT axial slices for each stone. RESULTS: No association was found between HUs and HV in UA stones (r=0.10, p=0.82); however, in COM stones, HUs correlated inversely and strongly with HV (r=−0.91, p=0.002). Further, we found a positive (r=0.37) but non-statistically significant (p=0.21) correlation between perceived fragmentation difficulty and mean Vickers hardness. CONCLUSIONS: Utilizing HUs as a proxy for mechanical hardness should not be done in isolation and must be interpreted in the context of stone composition. For COM stones, higher HUs reflect denser, preferentially oriented crystallites with reduced organic matrices, conditions that promote cleavage-controlled microcracking under indentation. Consequently, HUs, a volumetric voxel average, can increase as HV, a localized, defect-sensitive measure, decreases. More critically, our results indicate that Vickers hardness does not, in practice, reliably align with the surgeon's perception of fragmentation difficulty, prompting further analysis from our group, including microCT and nanoindentation.

title: GG01-11: Effect of High-Fat Diet on Radiation Response in bladder cancer: An In Vivo Study
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Obesity and high-fat diets (HFD) have been associated with tumor progression, immune modulation and reduced responsive to various therapies, including radiotherapy (RT). However, their specific influence on radiation response in bladder cancer remains underexplored. Our objective was to investigate the impact of a HFD on tumor growth and RT efficacy in a murine model. METHODS: 60 mice were randomized to a HFD or control diet (CTL) following acclimatization. They were subsequently injected with subcutaneously in the flank, with the MB49 murine bladder cancer cell line. Upon tumor volumes (TV) reaching 0.15cm3, mice were further stratified to either receive a single fraction of 10 Gy radiation to the tumor versus observation, yielding 4 cohorts: HFD-RT, HFD-Control, CTL-RT and CTL-Control. TV and mice body weight (BW) were monitored at regular intervals until TV reached 2.0cm3. Shapiro-Wilk Test was used to assess normal distribution. Pairwise Mann-Whitney U analysis done using R-Studio Software Version 12.1 2024. RESULTS: RT significantly decreased TV in the CTL group (CTLRT vs CTLCTL: 820.3 ± 505.4 mm3vs 1467.9 ± 734.8 mm3, p0.028) confirming the effect of a single fraction of 10Gy. However, in the HFD cohort, no statistical difference noted between the treatment and control arm (HFDRT2 vs HFDCTL: 1397.0 ± 600.8 mm3vs 1390.9 ± 740.4 mm3, p=0.86) elucidating the notion that HFD possibly increases tumor resistance to RT, which was also observed when comparison between the HFDRT and CTLRT shows a statistical difference in TV (p0.038).Despite expectations, HFD alone did not result in a greater BW at endpoint compared to the CTL (p0.78). However, BW loss following RT was significant in the control fed mice (CTLRT vs CTLCTL, p0.012), while no significant change in BW was observed in the HFD treated with RT compared to their respective controls. (HFDRT vs HFDCTL, p0.28), These results may suggest that the high-fat diet potentially mitigates the BW loss typically induced by radiation therapy. CONCLUSIONS: A HFD appears to attenuate the therapeutic efficacy of RT in an in vivo bladder cancer murine model. These findings suggest the hypothesis that dietary factors modulate tumor response to radiation and may have implications for treatment strategies in patients.

title: GG01-13: A Comparative Analysis of Prostatic Urethral Lift and Water Vapour Thermal Therapy for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia on Post-procedural Medication Cessation and Unplanned Readmissions
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1

speakers.organization: Sh Ho Urology Centre, The Chinese University of Hong Kong

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Minimally invasive surgical therapies (MIST) are increasingly adopted for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) due to their favorable safety and functional preservation profiles. This study aims to compare the drug-free status and complication rates of Prostatic Urethral Lift (PUL) and Water Vapour Thermal Therapy (WVTT). METHODS: We identified patients aged 50 years or older with prostate volumes of 30-80 cc who underwent either PUL or WVTT from January 2021 to December 2024. To ensure comparability, the cohorts were matched using 1:3 propensity score matching. Additional multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted on the entire pre-matched population. The primary outcome is the attainment of a drug-free status, defined as the discontinuation of both alpha-blockers and 5-alpha reductase inhibitors at the 6-month follow-up. The secondary outcome is unplanned readmissions within 30-day post-procedure. RESULTS: The analysis included 421 eligible patients (363 WVTT; 58 PUL). Baseline characteristics of the patients before and after matching are summarized in Table 1. Following propensity score matching (174 WVTT; 58 PUL), the PUL procedure was associated with a significantly greater likelihood of achieving drug-free status at 6 months compared to WVTT (weighted OR: 2.62, \[95% CI: 1.22-5.61\], p=0.013). This association persisted in the multivariable regression analysis (adjusted OR: 2.41 \[95% CI: 1.31–4.58\], p=0.006). There is no statistically significant difference in 30-day readmission rates between the groups in either the propensity score (p=0.097) or multivariable analysis (p=0.123), possibly due to the low number of readmission events (WVTT: 30; PUL: 5). Both MIST options exhibited an excellent safety profile, with no reinterventions recorded within the first year. Subgroup analyses consistently demonstrates superior drug-free outcome for PUL in patients with prostate size >50cc (OR 3.68, 95% CI 1.50–9.02, p=0.004), catheter-dependent patients (OR 2.54, 95% CI 1.13–5.70, p=0.024), and in cases without median lobe treatment (OR 2.53, 95% CI 1.18–5.43, p=0.018). CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates a statistically significant advantage for PUL over WVTT in enabling patients to discontinue BPH medications at six months, positioning PUL as a compelling MIST option with comparable safety progile for patients prioritizing cessation of medication. | | | --- | | |

title: GG01-15: Predictive Modelling of Functional Outcomes in HoLEP Versus Monopolar TURP: A Randomized Trial with ROC and Multivariate Statistical Analysis in Large-Volume BPH
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Large-volume BPH (>60 g) poses operative challenges due to bleeding and incomplete resection risk during monopolar TURP. HoLEP offers a size-independent, hemostatic alternative. This randomized trial compared HoLEP and monopolar TURP in prostates >60 g, incorporating ROC-based predictive modelling of postoperative voiding outcomes. METHODS: A prospective, block-randomized study included 120 men with symptomatic BPH and prostate volume >60 g, randomized to HoLEP (n=60) or monopolar TURP (n=60). Primary endpoints were perioperative hemoglobin change, catheterization duration, and hospital stay. Functional outcomes (Qmax, PVR, IPSS) were assessed at 1, 3, and 6 months. ROC analysis evaluated ΔQmax as a predictor of successful voiding. Multivariate regression adjusted for age, prostate volume, and baseline Qmax. RESULTS: Baseline demographics and symptom indices were comparable. HoLEP demonstrated reduced hemoglobin drop and shorter catheterization and hospitalization (mean stay 1.5 ± 0.4 vs 2.3 ± 0.6 days; p<0.01). Operative duration was modestly longer with HoLEP (81.6 ± 9.7 vs 74.9 ± 10.3 min; p=0.03). At 6 months, both groups improved significantly, with greater improvement in the HoLEP group (ΔQmax 10.2 ± 3.6 vs 7.9 ± 3.1 ml/s; p=0.02). HoLEP independently predicted higher postoperative flow (β=0.39; p=0.01) and reduced PVR (β=–0.35; p=0.02). ROC analysis showed stronger predictive accuracy for HoLEP (AUC 0.83; 95% CI 0.75–0.90; p<0.001) than TURP (AUC 0.70; 95% CI 0.61–0.81; p=0.01). Optimal ΔQmax cutoff≥14 ml/s yielded sensitivity/specificity of 82%/76% for HoLEP versus 69%/64% for TURP. CONCLUSIONS: In prostates >60 g, HoLEP demonstrates superior perioperative safety and improved early urinary flow outcomes compared with monopolar TURP, with equivalent symptom relief. Multivariate and ROC-based modelling confirms HoLEP as a more reliable predictor of durable voiding success in large-volume BPH. HoLEP represents a robust, size-independent therapeutic option in centers with established expertise.

title: GG01-16: Level of Circulating Cell-Free DNA in Urinary Bladder Cancer After Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour : A Prospective Observational Study
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1

speakers.organization: Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education And Research, Chandigarh

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) is the standard diagnostic and therapeutic procedure for bladder cancer. However, concerns regarding tumour cell dissemination during surgery persist. Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has emerged as a promising minimally invasive biomarker for cancer detection, treatment response, and post-treatment surveillance. This study aimed to measure changes in cfDNA levels before and after TURBT in patients with newly diagnosed primary bladder cancer and to correlate these changes with tumor grade, stage, and pathological characteristics. METHODS: This prospective observational pilot study was conducted at a tertiary care center in northern India from July 2022 to December 2023. Fifty patients with newly diagnosed primary bladder tumours scheduled for TURBT and undergoing complete endoscopic resection were enrolled. Peripheral blood samples were obtained preoperatively and 2 hours postoperatively. cfDNA was extracted using a commercially available plasma DNA extraction kit, and concentrations were quantified using a standard spectrophotometric method. Statistical analysis utilized paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test, while associations with clinicopathologic variables were evaluated using Spearman correlation and chi-square tests. RESULTS: The median pre-TURBT cfDNA level was 4.18 ng/mL (IQR 1.90–8.80), and the median post-TURBT level was 4.20 ng/mL (IQR 2.18–9.46), with no significant overall change. Significant increases in cfDNA were observed in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (p<0.0005), high-grade tumors (p<0.0007), and stage II–III disease (p<0.05). No significant association was observed between cfDNA change and operative duration >60 minutes. The cohort consisted primarily of older males, most presenting with painless gross hematuria and common risk factors such as smoking and occupational exposures. CONCLUSIONS: cfDNA levels appear influenced predominantly by tumor biology, including grade and stage rather than the TURBT procedure itself. cfDNA demonstrates potential as a non-invasive biomarker reflecting tumor aggressiveness and may complement histopathologic assessment in bladder cancer management. Larger studies are warranted to validate its clinical utility.

title: GG01-17: Diagnostic Performance of 68GA-PSMA-PET and MpMRI Fusion Based Targeted-  Cognitive Biopsy in Patients with Suspected Prostate Cancer: A Pilot Study
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Prostate cancer (PCa) diagnosis remains challenging due to the limited specificity of PIRADS 3–5 lesions on multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), often leading to unnecessary biopsies. Improved imaging techniques that enhance lesion characterisation and localisation could optimize biopsy yield. This pilot study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of 68Ga-PSMA-PET and mpMRI fusion-based cognitive targeted biopsy in detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) for improving biopsy accuracy. METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted at AIIMS, New Delhi,between July 2022 to August 2025. A total of 66 patients with suspicious lesions (PIRADS≥3) on multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA) of more than 4 and less than 20 ng/ml were enrolled after informed consent. Patients with clinically palpable disease on DRE, prior prostate surgery or pelvic radiation were excluded. All enrolled patients underwent PSMA PET/CT also before biopsy followed by software based fusion of PSMA-PET CT and MpMRI. All the patients underwent targeted biopsy based on MpMRI and fused PSMA-PET/MR image suspected lesions along with systematic 12 core TRUS fusion biopsy. The primary objective was to evaluate the accuracy of fused PSMA-PET/MRI image targeted biopsy in diagnosing clinically significant prostate cancer, secondary objective includes overall cancer detection accuracy. RESULTS: The study included 66 male patients with suspected prostate carcinoma and serum PSA levels between 4-20 ng/mL. The mean age was 63 ± 6.8 years and mean serum PSA was 8.05 ± 4.4 ng/mL. Imaging assessments using fused 68Ga PSMA-PET/MRI reveals notable diagnostic performance, particularly for clinically significant prostate cancer. The modality exhibits a high sensitivity of 96 %, specificity of 79 % and a positive predictive value (PPV) of 76.4 %. The negative predictive value (NPV) was 96.8 %, indicating that fused 68Ga PSMA-PET/MRI targeted biopsy has a high sensitivity for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer than MRI targeted alone. These results suggest that 68Ga PSMA-PET/MRI fusion could be an effective tool for guiding targeted biopsies in patients with elevated PSA levels and suspected prostate cancer. CONCLUSIONS: Our study underscores the clinical potential of 68Ga-PSMA-PET/MRI fused image as a powerful diagnostic tool in the evaluation of patients with suspected prostate cancer. By integrating the molecular specificity of PSMA-PET with the superior anatomical resolution of multiparametric MRI, this hybrid approach enables more accurate differentiation between clinically significant and insignificant prostate cancers, reducing the number of unnecessary biopsies and minimizing patient morbidity, procedural risks, and healthcare costs. The high negative predictive value (NPV) observed with fused 68Ga-PSMA-PET/MRI targeted biopsy supports its role as a reliable pre-biopsy triage modality. Moreover, in resource-limited settings where integrated PET/MRI systems are not readily available, software-based fusion of PSMA-PET/CT and mpMRI represents a feasible and cost-effective alternative for targeted biopsy guidance.

title: GG01-18: Effects of Oral Vitamin D Supplementation in an Experimental Model of Peyronie’s Disease
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1

speakers.jobTitle: Fellow of European Committee of Sexual Medicine

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Despite several proposed treatments, the underlying molecular mechanisms of fibrosis and potential modulatory therapies of Peyronie's Disease (PD) remain unclear. Recent evidence suggests that vitamin D (vitD) may play a regulatory role in extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammation, and fibrosis, offering a potential therapeutic pathway for PD. We aimed to evaluate effects of vitD supplementation in an experimental model of PD. METHODS: Thirty-six male Wistar rats were divided into groups: control (G1), induced PD and placebo (G2) and induced PD plus oral vitD supplementation (G3). PD was induced by TA injection of autologous plasma according to a validated model. VitD was administered orally for 8 or 18 weeks, corresponding to the acute and chronic phases. Collagens I and III were quantified by Picrosirius Red staining and VitD receptor expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry. RESULTS: During the acute phase, type I collagen content did not differ significantly among groups (p=0.91), nor did type III collagen (p=0.54). In the chronic phase, Group 1 showed lower collagen I (12.4 ± 8.4%) and higher collagen III (38.7 ± 6.4%) compared to G2 and G3, though not statistically significant (p=0.27). In the chronic phase, G2 exhibited a higher type I/III collagen ratio compared to treated group (G3), indicating a more fibrotic tunical pattern, whereas vitD administration may be associated with a shift toward a less fibrotic, more regenerative matrix profile. ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191268.85865.a2.18#F1)) VitD receptor expression did not differ significantly among groups in the acute phase; however, in the chronic phase, both mean H-score and stained area percentage were significantly higher in Group 3 than in Groups 1 and 2 (p<0.05), indicating upregulated vitD receptor expression ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191268.85865.a2.18#F2)). CONCLUSIONS: VitD supplementation was associated with upregulation of VitD receptor expression and a reduced type I/III collagen ratio in the tunica albuginea, suggesting attenuation of chronic fibrosis and preservation of a more regenerative matrix profile. These findings support a potential antifibrotic role of vitD in PD.

title: GG01-19: Finasteride 1 mg: Silent Impacts on Male Fertility Despite Preserved Hormonal Balance
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Finasteride, a type-2 5α-reductase inhibitor, is prescribed for benign prostatic hyperplasia and androgenetic alopecia. Effects on male fertility remains uncertain. This study aimed to assess the impact of finasteride 1 mg/day on semen parameters, hormonal profiles, sexual function, and psychological status in men of reproductive age. METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional case-control study was approved by the Institutional Review Board (No. 92540525.0.0000.0068) and included 465 men aged 18–60 years (69 finasteride users and 396 controls). Semen analyses followed WHO 2021 criteria. Hormones measured included total and free testosterone (TT, FT), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), estradiol (E2), sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), prolactin (PRL), cortisol, and dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Metabolic (glucose, HbA1c, lipids, 25-hydroxyvitamin D) and thyroid parameters were also assessed. Sexual and psychological status were evaluated using the International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-15), quantitative Androgen Deficiency in the Aging Male (qADAM), Male Sexual Quotient (MSQ), Beck Depression and Anxiety Inventories (BDI, BAI), Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAM-A), and Montgomery–Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS). Univariate comparisons and multivariate linear regression were adjusted for covariates. Statistical significance was set at p<0.05. RESULTS: Mean age 41.9 ± 8.4 years; BMI 27.1 ± 3.9 kg/m2. Finasteride users had similar metabolic and hormonal profiles, except for higher HDL cholesterol (49.7 ± 8.7 vs. 46.1 ± 10.6 mg/dL; p=0.025). Mean duration of finasteride treatment was 73.5 ± 72.0 months. Semen quality was reduced in finasteride users: sperm concentration 55.6 ± 58.3 vs. 90.6 ± 93.8 ×106/mL, total sperm count 151.9 ± 205.1 vs. 254.1 ± 258.9 ×106/ejaculate, and total motile sperm count 72.6 ± 79.8 vs. 166.6 ± 182.9 ×106(all p0.001). Sperm morphology Kruger (2.0 ± 2.7 vs. 3.9 ± 4.0%) and WHO criteria (9.0 ± 8.2 vs. 14.9 ± 9.7%). Multivariate regression confirmed finasteride as an independent predictor of lower sperm concentration (=−26.9; p=0.025), total sperm count (=−72.9; p=0.031), total motile sperm count (=−75.7; p=0.002), and sperm morphology (=−4.18; p=0.002). DHT was lower (0.17 ± 0.20 vs. 0.58 ± 0.49 ng/mL; p0.001), but TT, FT, FSH, LH, and E2 were similar between groups. Questionnaire analyses showed mild, nonsignificant declines in erectile function and vitality. Sexual satisfaction, mood, urinary, and stress scores were comparable. CONCLUSIONS: Finasteride 1 mg/day reduces significantly sperm production and morphology without affecting endocrine, sexual, or psychological function.

title: GG01-20: Compensated hypogonadism and sperm DNA fragmentation in men with sickle cell disease: impact on semen parameters
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1

speakers.organization: Universidade Estadual de Feira de Santana

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Men with sickle cell disease (SCD) may have impaired fertility due to chronic systemic burden, vaso-occlusive injury, and treatment-related toxicity, even when conventional semen parameters appear normal. Hormonal alterations and oxidative stress can compromise spermatogenesis and sperm DNA integrity. Compensated hypogonadism, defined by normal testosterone with elevated LH, may represent early endocrine dysfunction, but its impact on sperm DNA fragmentation (DFI) in SCD is poorly characterized. We aimed to evaluate semen parameters, sperm DNA integrity, and hormonal profile in adult men with SCD, focusing on the association between compensated hypogonadism and unfavorable seminal outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study including 37 adult men with SCD (median age 38 years; IQR 29–44) followed at a reference hematology center. Semen analysis was performed according to WHO 2021 guidelines. DFI was measured by flow cytometry using a validated protocol. Serum total testosterone, FSH, LH, and AMH were assessed. Structured interviews collected demographic, clinical, and reproductive data. Compensated hypogonadism was defined as total testosterone >300 ng/dL with LH≥9.4 mIU/mL. Statistical analyses included correlation tests and subgroup comparisons between eugonadal and compensated hypogonadal men. RESULTS: Of 37 participants, 25 (67.5%) completed semen analysis; four declined for religious reasons. Median sperm concentration was 23.4 million/mL, median DFI was 28% (IQR 12–49), and median strict morphology was 1%. All men had total testosterone >300 ng/dL, while 30% met criteria for compensated hypogonadism. This subgroup showed significantly lower total motile sperm count (median 3.45 vs 26.4 million; p<0.05) and higher DFI (49.5% vs 15%; p<0.01). DFI was moderately and significantly correlated with strict morphology (r=–0.57; 95% CI –0.82 to –0.14; p=0.013). Given the small sample size, no clear pattern emerged regarding hydroxyurea exposure and semen parameters or DFI. CONCLUSIONS: Despite normal serum testosterone, compensated hypogonadism in men with SCD was associated with poorer semen quality and markedly higher sperm DNA fragmentation, indicating that reproductive dysfunction may occur before a measurable decline in circulating testosterone. These findings support routine reproductive evaluation and early fertility counseling in men with SCD, even in the absence of overt hypogonadism, and highlight the potential role of DFI assessment beyond standard semen analysis.

title: GG01-21: Artificial intelligence–derived tumor volume in multiparametric MRI: validation and multimodal applications for nodal and extracapsular extension prediction in prostate cancer
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Tumor volume is a key prognostic factor in prostate cancer, associated with extracapsular extension (ECE), nodal invasion (pN+), and recurrence. Artificial intelligence (AI) applied to multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) enables objective and reproducible volume quantification, potentially improving preoperative risk stratification. This study aimed to validate AI-derived tumor volume against histopathology and evaluate its integration into multimodal predictive models for nodal and extracapsular extension. METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 102 patients who underwent radical prostatectomy with extended pelvic lymph node dissection and preoperative mpMRI and PSMA PET/CT between 2021–2024 was analyzed. Tumor volume was automatically calculated from mpMRI using a convolutional neural network–based segmentation algorithm integrated into the mdprostate© platform (Mediaire GmbH, Germany). Pathological volume was obtained from surgical specimens. Correlation between AI-estimated and pathological volumes was assessed with Pearson and Spearman coefficients. AI-derived variables (tumor volume and tumor density \[tumor\ volume/prostate volume\]) were integrated into two logistic regression models: (1) a nodal model, combining tumor density and PET-PSMA SUVmax, compared with the Briganti nomogram; and (2) an ECE model, incorporating MRI-based ECE status, AI-derived tumor density, and SUVmax, benchmarked against mpMRI alone. Model performance was evaluated by AUC, calibration, and diagnostic metrics using SPSS v29.0. RESULTS: AI-derived tumor volume strongly correlated with pathological volume (r=0.71; ρ=0.68; p<0.001), with a systematic underestimation (bias –5.8 ml). In multivariable analysis, tumor density (OR 1.15; p=0.03) and SUVmax (OR 1.06; p=0.02) were independent predictors of nodal invasion. The multimodal nodal model achieved an AUC of 0.870 (95% CI 0.801–0.940), outperforming Briganti (AUC 0.740) and reducing indicated lymphadenectomies by ≈6% at equivalent sensitivity (97%). For ECE prediction, MRI ECE (OR 7.77; p<0.001), tumor density (OR 1.13; p=0.03), and SUVmax (OR 1.06; p=0.02) were independent predictors. The AI-based model outperformed mpMRI (AUC 0.823 vs 0.761), reducing false negatives from 29.2% to 21.7% and false positives from 19.2% to 13.7%, improving surgical planning accuracy in ≈7% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: AI-derived tumor volume is a validated quantitative biomarker that enhances the prediction of nodal and extracapsular extension when combined with MRI and PET-PSMA parameters. This multimodal approach supports more individualized and precise surgical decision-making. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: GG01-22: Epidemiology and Regional Variation in Prostate Cancer Incidence and Treatment in Hungary
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Prostate cancer (PCa) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among European men. Most epidemiological evidence originates from Western countries, yet substantial variation may exist in smaller nations such as Hungary due to differences in population risk, screening, and treatment practices. We therefore conducted a comprehensive national assessment of PCa epidemiology and management in Hungary. METHODS: Data from the National Health Insurance Fund, Hungarian Central Statistical Office, National Cancer Registry, and WHO were used to calculate crude, age-specific, and age-standardized incidence and mortality rates. County-level analyses assessed regional variation in incidence and the use of radical prostatectomy (RP) and definitive radiotherapy (RT). Analyses were performed in GraphPad Prism. RESULTS: Between 2001 and 2022, the crude incidence of PCa in Hungary increased from 55.7 to 102.3 cases per 100,000 men, with a peak observed in 2017, followed by a transient decline. Since 2012, age-standardized incidence rates have remained stable, whereas crude rates continued to rise gradually. Age-specific incidence increased steadily with advancing age, peaking at 642 cases per 100,000 men aged≥80 years in 2022. The largest relative contribution to total cases occurred in the 60–69-year age group. Regionally, Budapest showed the highest crude incidence (113 per 100,000). County-level data revealed wide regional variation, with RP rates ranging from –37% to +51% and RT rates from –38% to +72% relative to the national mean. Some areas, like Komárom-Esztergom County, fell well below average in both RP (–27%) and RT (–37%). RP and RT rates reached about 20% and 15% of the national prostate cancer incidence, respectively. While age-standardized mortality declined from approximately 60 to 40 deaths per 100,000 men (annual percent change: –0.97% per year; 95% CI: –1.49% to –0.46%), crude mortality increased gradually, and age-specific mortality remained stable across all age groups. The age-standardized mortality-to-incidence ratio remained around 0.33 (2012-2022), temporarily exceeding 0.40 during COVID-19. CONCLUSIONS: PCa in Hungary is underdiagnosed, with most cases detected at older ages and stark regional variation, which may reflect differences in healthcare access. Limited screening and uneven availability of curative treatments lead to delayed detection and lower intervention rates outside wealthier regions. These findings underscore the need for further research to clarify drivers of variation and to support efforts toward earlier detection and broader access to high-quality PCa care in Hungary.

title: GG01-23: Testosterone Responsiveness as a Predictive Biomarker of Successful Sperm Retrieval in Non-Obstructive Azoospermia
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1

speakers.organization: American University of Beirut Medical Center

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether testosterone responsiveness to pre-operative hormonal therapy predicts successful sperm retrieval (SSR) after microsurgical testicular sperm extraction (micro-TESE) in men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA), and to define hormonal and operative parameters that may improve surgical outcomes. METHODS: A retrospective review of 77 NOA patients who underwent micro-TESE was performed. Demographic, clinical, and hormonal data (FSH, LH, testosterone, estradiol, prolactin, TSH) were recorded pre-and post-hormonal therapy (oral or injectables). The testosterone response (ΔT=post – pre testosterone) and therapy route (oral vs. injectable) were correlated with SSR, operative time, and IVF outcomes. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of SSR. RESULTS: The overall SSR rate was 46.7%. Patients with positive retrieval had significantly higher post-therapy testosterone (771 vs 464ng/dL; p=0.003), greater ΔT (478 vs 245ng/dL; p=0.026), and shorter operative time (99 vs 121 min; p<0.001). Oral hormonal regimens achieved higher SSR than injectables (56.8% vs 33.3%; p=0.054). On multivariable analysis, both post-therapy testosterone and ΔT independently predicted SSR (p<0.05). Pregnancy and live-birth rates after successful retrieval were 41.6%. CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic testosterone response following hormonal therapy serves as an independent predictor of sperm retrieval success in NOA. Incorporating ΔT into pre-operative evaluation may help identify candidates most likely to benefit from micro-TESE. These results support testosterone responsiveness as a true biomarker for precision fertility surgery.

title: GG01-24: A composite biomarker approach to withhold neoadjuvant chemotherapy in select muscle-invasive bladder cancer patients
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) prior to radical cystectomy (RC) is recommended for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC). However, we propose a composite biomarker approach of circulating tumor cell status and gene expression to select patients in whom NAC may be omitted. METHODS: Transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) samples were collected from patients with cT2-T4aN0-N1M0 MIBC who were included in the prospective CirGuidance study (NL3954), in which circulating tumor cells (CTC) were enumerated using the CELLSEARCH® system. Expression profiling was performed using the validated Decipher Bladder genomic subtyping classifier to determine luminal and non-luminal molecular subtypes (Veracyte, Inc.). The luminal favorable subtype was determined using a lncRNA-based classifier (de Jong et al. 2019 and 2024). The primary endpoint was cancer-specific mortality (CSM), calculated from the date of study inclusion to the date of bladder cancer related death. RESULTS: In the CirGuidance study (n=231), most patients (n=213; 92%) underwent RC without NAC, while (n=18) received NAC plus RC. Among RC-only patients, CTCneg status (n=172) was associated with a two-year CSM of 21% versus 41% in CTCpos patients (Gray’s test, p=0.01). No significant differences were observed in the distribution of molecular subtypes between CTCpos or CTCneg patient subgroups. Within CTCneg patients treated with RC alone, 2-year CSM was 14% in luminal (n=77, 36%) versus 25% in non-luminal (n=136, 64%) whereas in CTCpos patients it was 38% and 44%, respectively. Among 18 NAC plus RC treated patients, non-luminal subtype (n=10) had a two-year CSM of 11%, whereas in luminal subtype it was 27%, similar to outcomes when treated with RC alone. Importantly, the lncRNA-based luminal favorable classifier identified 26 patients with luminal favorable subtype among CTCneg patients with 0% CSM at two years (MVA p=0.02) when treated with RC alone. CONCLUSIONS: We identified a biomarker-defined subgroup of MIBC with more favorable outcomes after RC alone. These findings support the future prospective validation of CTC and molecular subtyping as a tool to guide NAC selection.

title: GG01-25: Beyond the Scalpel: Evaluation of the Paclitaxel Drug-Coated-Balloon as an Alternative to Open Urethroplasty at a Tertiary Referral Center: Two year follow-up data
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Patients with recurrent bulbar urethral stricture≤3 cm have been offered treatment with Paclitaxel Drug-Coated-Balloon (DCB) as an alternative to open urethroplasty at our centre since December 2022. The objective of this study is to evaluate the success rate of DCB treatment. METHODS: All patients treated with DCB from December 2022-March 2024 were included in this retrospective single-centre study. All patients follow a standardized treatment and follow-up (FU). All patients were evaluated with retrograde urethrogram and urethroscopy at baseline and when indicated during FU. We record IPSS score, USS-PROM, IIEF-5, and uroflowmetry preoperatively, and at FU at 3-, 12-month and annually up to 5 years postoperatively. The primary endpoint is the need for retreatment. Secondary endpoints include changes in Qmax, residual urine, IPSS score, USS-PROM, quality of life and erectile function. RESULTS: 111 men with a median age of 42 years (range 18–82) were included. 100 patients (90%) had a bulbar stricture, 11 (10%) had a bulbomembranousstricture. Prior treatments included direct vision internal urethrotomy (DVIU) (N=102), urethroplasty (N=15), and 15% of the patients performed Clean Intermittend Catheterization (CIC)/selfdilatation at some point. Etiology was mostly idiopathic or unknown (N=95), and median stricture length was 10 mm (range 2–32). Median Qmax at baseline was 8.1 (2.1-30). Adverse events following treatment included haematuria (20%), including one transfusion-requiring haemorrhage (Hb 12 to 7), urinary tract infection (3.6%), and transient urinary retention after catheter removal (1%). All 111 patients have completed the 12-month FU. Median Qmax at 3-month FU was 21.5 (7.3-50) and 19 (4-50) at 12-month FU. Recurrent strictures, confirmed by urethrography, were found in 42/111 (38%) patients. Median time from treatment to recurrence was 12 months (4-24). So far, 39 of these have undergone retreatment: 29 urethroplasty, 5 redo-DCB, 1 DVIU, 4 simple dilations. Nine out of ten patients retreated with conservative methods had soft, short strictures. The rate of freedom from repeat intervention for all 111 patients after a median FU-time of 23 months (14-34months) is 62%. CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with DCB for recurrent bulbar urethral stricture is a safe and easy minimally invasive treatment with good short-term results, however success rates are lower than the gold standard treatment of urethroplasty.

title: GG01-26: High concentrations of pentoxifylline after capacitation impair bovine sperm function and in vitro fertilization outcomes
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: In vitro embryo production (IVP) is an essential biotechnology for genetic dissemination and herd productivity. However, cryopreserved semen often compromises fertilization efficiency. Pentoxifylline (PTX), a phosphodiesterase inhibitor, enhances sperm motility in several species and may mitigate cryodamage. This study evaluated whether post-capacitation supplementation with 10 or 20 mm PTX affects sperm function and in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes in cattle. METHODS: The study was conducted at a Brazilian Animal Biotechnology and Reproduction Laboratory using semen from four Nelore bulls. Samples were thawed, processed by Percoll gradient (45–90%), and divided into three groups: G1) control, G2) 10 mm PTX, and G3) 20 mm PTX. Sperm motility, vigor, mitochondrial activity, capacitation status, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were assessed. Data were analyzed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test (p<0.05). RESULTS: Comparing G1 (control), G2 (10 mm PTX), and G3 (20 mm PTX), respectively, post-thaw motility was 51.56 ± 1.54, 51.56 ± 1.54, and 51.56 ± 1.54 (p=1.00), and vigor 2.68 ± 0.08, 2.68 ± 0.08, and 2.68 ± 0.08 (p=1.00). After capacitation, motility declined to 29.53 ± 2.90A, 20.18 ± 2.86B, and 14.62 ± 2.21B(p<0.0001), while vigor dropped to 2.25 ± 0.12A, 1.87 ± 0.12B, and 1.59 ± 0.11B(p=0.0002). PTX did not affect IVF rates (p=0.95) but reduced cleavage at 20 mm (p=0.01) and expanded blastocysts at 10 mm (p=0.04). Degenerative acrosomal reactions increased (p=0.0004), while mitochondrial activity and ROS levels showed no differences (p>0.05). Both PTX concentrations impaired sperm function and embryo development. CONCLUSIONS: PTX at 10 and 20 mm proved detrimental to bovine sperm function, reducing motility, vigor, and acrosomal integrity, and impairing cleavage and blastocyst formation. Although mitochondrial activity and oxidative stress were unchanged, the increased acrosomal degeneration suggests cytotoxicity at high doses. These findings indicate that PTX supplementation after capacitation does not enhance IVF outcomes and may impair sperm performance in a dose-dependent, species-specific manner. Further studies should determine safe concentrations that improve motility without compromising fertilization or embryonic development.

title: GG01-27: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF SHEAR WAVE ELASTOGRAPHY FOR RISK STRATIFICATION OF PATIENTS WITH ERECTILE DYSFUNCTION—A PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is the most common male sexual dysfunction and its prevalence is increasing year after year. The best method to predict the severity of ED is histological assessment of the penile tissue through biopsy. However, its role is limited because of its complexity, invasiveness, and associated serious side effects. Elastography is a new and non-invasive imaging modality used for assessing the stiffness of tissues. Here we aim to find out the penile viscoelasticity(stiffness) of corpora cavernosa with the new and non-invasive diagnostic Shear wave elastography (SWE) and correlate it with the IIEF-5 score. METHODS: We included patients aged18-70 years with erectile dysfunction who are willing to participate in the study. The exclusion criteria are Peyronie's disease, penile trauma, spinal injury, h/o penile surgery, severe psychiatric disorder, patients not willing to undergo SWE, patients with hypogonadism, and carcinoma penis. All included patients were divided into 4 categories according to IIEF-5 scoring (Control-22-25, Mild ED-17-21, Moderate ED-8-16, and Severe ED-5-7). They underwent shear wave elastography of Bilateral corpora cavernosa in flaccid penis in proximal and distal parts separately. They were followed up after 3 months with being treated with PDE5i. The IIEF-5 scores were assessed after 3 months. RESULTS: We evaluated 41 patients (Severe ED-8, Moderate ED-8, Mild ED-9, Control-14) with penile SWE in bilateral corpora cavernosa both proximal and distal part in flaccid penis. From the initiation of the study, we found the mean SWE of patients with severe, moderate and mild ED were 29.14(Standard Deviation 4.0) KPa, 20.08(SD 4.0) KPa and 17.7(SD 4.1) KPa respectively. The mean SWE of normal/control patients without ED is 15.28(SD 3.9) KPa. Patients with mild and moderate with low mean SWE values responded well to PDE5i with 3 months follow up. CONCLUSIONS: This SWE will be a non-invasive objective method which could be highly beneficial from the clinical practice standpoint compared with other modalities like colour Doppler which require intra-cavernosal injection to assess the ED. Our method might have great potential to make a paradigm shift in both the diagnosis and prognosis of ED. This study will be the first of its kind to be undertaken among Indian population.

title: GG01-28: Urban–Rural Disparities in Prostate Cancer Outcomes: A Nationwide Population-Based Analysis
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most common malignancy among Brazilian men, but regional disparities in access to screening and treatment may influence disease burden. Understanding differences between urban and rural regions is crucial for planning equitable public health strategies. Objective: To analyze temporal trends and regional disparities in PCa incidence, mortality, and mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR) in Brazil, comparing urbanized and less urbanized regions. METHODS: Population-based data from DATASUS and INCA (2013–2021) were analyzed for men aged≥50 years. Age-specific incidence (PCSIR) and mortality (PCSMR) rates per 10,000 inhabitants were calculated. Regions were classified by degree of urbanization and healthcare infrastructure. Non-parametric Wilcoxon tests compared regional medians, and Joinpoint regression identified temporal trends. Multivariate robust linear regression models assessed associations between MIR and healthcare accessibility indicators (number of treatment centers, GDP per capita, urbanization index, and PSA screening coverage). RESULTS: A total of 273,933 new cases and 135,336 deaths were recorded. Median PCSIR was highest in the Southeast (14.7/10,000) and lowest in the North (6.9/10,000), representing a 113% higher incidence in the most urbanized region. Conversely, MIR was twice as high in the North (0.88) compared to the Southeast (0.44). The Northeast showed the highest mortality (7.7/10,000), 28% higher than the South (6.0/10,000). Joinpoint analysis revealed an incidence rise until 2018 (β=+3.66, p<0.001) followed by a post-2020 decline (β=−2.15, p=0.002). In multivariate models, higher MIR was independently associated with lower urbanization (β=−0.43, p=0.01) and reduced access to radiotherapy and robotic surgery (β=−0.35, p=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: Urban regions in Brazil exhibit higher PCa incidence due to greater screening coverage, while rural and less urbanized regions show higher mortality and MIR, reflecting delayed diagnosis and limited treatment access. Strengthening early detection and expanding oncologic infrastructure in rural areas are essential to reduce inequalities in PCa outcome

title: GG01-29: Penile Girth Enhancement using Hyaluronic Acid Filler: A Prospective Evaluation of 120 patients
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1

speakers.organization: INSTITUTO DE UROLOGIA E ANDROLGIA DR LEONARDO DE SOUZA ALVES

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Penile girth enhancement has gained increasing attention among men seeking aesthetic and functional impromvement. Among available techniques hyaluronic acid (HA) filler injections have emerged as minimally invasive and reversible alternative to surgical augmentation. HA fillers are biocompative and absorbable, offering immediate results with favorable safety profile. However, objective data regarding the magnitude and durability of penile girth increase remain limited. Objective of this is evaluate the efficacy and short term persistence of penile girth enhancement using hyaluronic acid filler injections in men seeking penile augmentation. METHODS: A total of 120 men aged 25-55 years underwent penile augmentation with 8-12 ml of cross linked hyaluronic acid (HA). The product was injected subdermally along the penile shaft using a cannula technique. All procedures were perfomed by same urologist, under local anesthesia in a outpatient setting. Penile circumference was measured at the mid-shaft in the flaccid state at four time points: 15 minutes post-procedure, 15, 45, and 3 months. RESULTS: Immediate increase (15 minutes): mean gain of 2,0-3,0 cm in penile circumference. At 15 days: addiitonal mean increase of 0,5 cm. At 45 days and 3 months: the girth increase remained stable, with no significant reduction in circumference compared to the 15 day measurement. Adverse event with ecchymosis in 9% of patients, no cases of infection, no nodules, no vascular complications. CONCLUSIONS: Penile girth enhancement with hyaluronic acid filler resulted in a significant and durable increase in penile circumference, maintained up to 3 months post procedure at least. The techinque demostraded a high safety profile, minimal downtime, and high patient satisfaction. Hyaluronic Acid injection represents a safe effective and reversible option for penile augmentation in men seeking aeshtetic or confidence-related improvement.

title: GG01-30: Automating Clavien-Dindo Classification with Large Language Models: a faster and more reliable way for data collection
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1

speakers.organization: Hospital das Clinicas HCFMUSP, Faculdade de Medicina, Universidade de Sao Paulo, Sao Paulo, SP, Brazil

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Interrater agreement of the Clavien-Dindo classification is only moderate, what questions the reliability of any conclusions that use it as a study endpoint. We aimed to validate the use of large language models (LLMs) for this task, benchmark them against physician performance, and compare the performance of different LLMs. METHODS: We evaluated the accuracy of ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek, Google Gemini, xAI Grok and Meta Llama through four steps: (1) defining Clavien-Dindo grades, (2) classifying complications, (3) classifying case summaries, and (4) classifying case summaries after machine learning. Vignettes were obtained from a categorization of percutaneous nephrolithotomy complications, used as an answer key. We measured agreement with Gwet’s AC2 coefficient and compared it with attending urologists and urology residents via electronic survey. RESULTS: All models accurately defined the Clavien-Dindo classification and accurately graded complication descriptions and case summaries before and after machine learning (accuracy values in Table 1). Six attending urologists and 15 residents classified the same vignettes, demonstrating lower accuracy than the LLMs (p<0.001). LLMs’ latency ranged from 1.04 (Copilot) to 3.02 minutes (DeepSeek), while the fastest physician required 17 minutes to complete the same tasks. LLMs’ intra-rater reliability was almost perfect: from 0.97 (Copilot) to 0.99 (Llama). Interrater reliability between LLMs (0.98, 95% CI: 0.97-0.98) was significantly higher than among physicians (0.93, 95% CI: 0.92-0.94). CONCLUSIONS: LLMs are faster, more accurate and more precise than physicians for Clavien-Dindo classification. We recommend its use to automate data collection, provided that it is implemented in compliance with applicable laws and ethical standards. We do not have evidence to endorse one specific LLM over another; this choice remains at the discretion of the user. | | | --- | | | | | | --- | | |

title: GG01-31: Profile of Brazilian Men Seeking Online Help for Ejaculatory Disorders
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1

speakers.jobTitle: MD PhD -  Head of the Medical Residency Program in Urology at Hospital São Luiz Jabaquara - Rede D´Or / IDOR - SP

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: This study describes the profile of Brazilian men seeking online help for premature ejaculation. METHODS: An online application was used to evaluate men with ejaculatory disorders. The study analyzed data from 1,242 Brazilian men collected between October 20, 2024, and March 22, 2025. Participation was voluntary, and informed consent was obtained. Responses were collected via a questionnaire in the app and analyzed with the aid of artificial intelligence. The prevalence of ejaculatory disorders was determined using global questions derived from the definitions in validated instruments (IELT and PEDT). This was an uncontrolled retrospective study conducted in accordance with the guidelines of the Brazilian Ministry of Health, the Declaration of Helsink. RESULTS: From October 20, 2024, to March 22, 2025, 1,242 men voluntarily completed the questionnaire. Ages ranged from 18 to 72 years (median, 32 years). Most participants lived in the Southeast (31.6%) or Northeast (29.5%) regions. Of the respondents, 75.7% had a stable partner, 36.6% had hypertension, and 12.6% had diabetes. The app was discovered primarily through YouTube (42.4%), Google (22.5%), and Instagram (17.5%); overall, 87.7% of users learned about it via these platforms. Sixty-six percent of the men had never sought treatment for any sexual complaint, yet 88% expressed a genuine desire to improve their sex lives. Prevalence of dysfunctions was as follows: 41.2% had both premature ejaculation (PE) and erectile dysfunction (ED), 30.0% had PE only, and 13.0% had ED only. The primary concerns were improving ejaculation control (60.9%) and improving erections (22.1%). Men with PE were 1.65 times more likely to have ED than men without PE (odds ratio). CONCLUSIONS: The study underscores the need for an integrated assessment of male sexual function that includes both ejaculatory control and erectile quality, particularly when one dysfunction is present. A multidisciplinary approach involving physicians and psychotherapists is recommended. The app is a valuable tool but cannot replace in-person multidisciplinary care.

title: GG01-32: Preemptive Analgesia Using Lidocaine Infiltration Before Incision in Subinguinal Varicocelectomy: Interim Analysis of a Double Blind Randomized Trial
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Microsurgical varicocelectomy (MSV) is the most commonly performed operation for male infertility. Although MSV is minimally invasive, postoperative pain remains a key concern for many patients. This study aimed to determine whether pre-emptive analgesia via local infiltration of 0.5% lidocaine before skin and cremaster incision provides more effective early pain control than the current standard technique of lidocaine infiltration after wound closure. METHODS: We conducted a triple-blinded randomized controlled trial with men undergoing left subinguinal microsurgical varicocelectomy that were randomized to: Group A (pre-emptive)—lidocaine 0.5% infiltrated before incision at skin and cremaster; saline after closure; or Group B (post-closure)—saline before incision; lidocaine 0.5% after closure. Pain assessed by Visual Analog Scale (VAS) was recorded at 1, 6, and 24 postoperative hours in rest and cough. The following endpoits were compared between groups: each patient’s mean of the six VAS scores within 24h, presence of any pain (≥1 evaluation with VAS>0), and clinically relevant pain (≥1 evaluation with VAS>3), each assessed overall (rest+cough) and separately (rest only; cough only) at 1h, 6h, 24h; plus any rescue analgesic use. RESULTS: We enrolled and randomized 29 men, 14 in the preemptive group (PG) and 15 in the contreol group n=15 (CG). Early postoperative pain was generally low and comparable: mean 24 h VAS in PG 1.63 vs CG 2.27 (p=0.34). Any pain within 24 h occurred in PG 71% vs CG 93% (p=0.169), with no significant differences at 1 h, 6 h, or 24 h; rest only analyses were similar (p=1.00), and cough only patterns mirrored overall with not significant trends favoring preemptive at 6 h and 24 h. Clinically relevant pain was PG 43% vs CG 73% over 24 h (p=0.139) without time specific significance; rescue analgesic use did not differ, PG 29% vs CG 40% (p=0.700), and opioids were rarely required, PG 0% vs CG 6.7% (p=1.00). CONCLUSIONS: Overall, early postoperative pain after microsurgical varicocelectomy was low, with a low need for rescue analgesics across both study arms. In these preliminary data, the number of clinically relevant pain episodes (VAS>3) and the proportion requiring any rescue analgesic were numerically higher in the post-closure lidocaine group than in the pre-emptive group, but none of these differences reached statistical significance. Taken together with the primary non-inferiority finding, these results suggest that pre-emptive local infiltration is at least an equivalent strategy for early analgesia; however, larger, adequately powered randomized trials are needed to define the true clinical benefit of this anesthetic approach.

title: GG01-33: Minimally Invasive Surgical Therapies Compared with Pharmacotherapy for Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Men with Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Minimally invasive surgical therapies (MISTs) have emerged as alternatives to long-term pharmacological treatment in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Their comparative effectiveness versus standard drug therapy remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared outcomes of MISTs and pharmacotherapy in men with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) secondary to BPH. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies comparing MISTs—water vapor thermal therapy (Rezum), prostatic artery embolization (PAE), and prostatic urethral lift (PUL)—with pharmacotherapy. Study selection followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Primary outcomes were the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) and maximum urinary flow rate (Qmax). Secondary outcomes included quality of life (QoL), sexual function, adverse events, and retreatment. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed, with subgroup analyses by MIST type. RESULTS: 3 RCTs and 2 Cohort including 475 men treated with MISTs and 1,876 treated with pharmacotherapy were analyzed. For IPSS, the overall meta-analysis found no significant difference between MISTs and pharmacotherapy (mean difference \[MD\] 2.17, 95% confidence interval \[CI\] –1.19 to 5.53; P=0.15; I2=91%). Subgroup analyses showed no significant differences for Rezum (MD 0.30, 95% CI –0.48 to 1.08; P=0.99), PAE (MD 0.00, 95% CI –11.32 to 11.33; P=0.99), or PUL (MD 4.53, 95% CI –15.90 to 24.95; P=0.22). For Qmax, no difference was observed (MD 0.33 ml/s, 95% CI –0.17 to 0.83; P=0.14; I2=0%), with no significant subgroup interaction (P=0.74). Secondary outcomes were inconsistently reported, limiting further quantitative synthesis. CONCLUSIONS: MISTs did not demonstrate superior efficacy to pharmacotherapy in symptom relief or urinary flow improvement. High heterogeneity among trials likely reflects differences in patient selection, prostate size, and follow-up duration. Current evidence suggests that MISTs offer equivalent efficacy but may represent a suitable alternative when drug intolerance, side effects, or patient preference are decisive. Additional well-designed RCTs with standardized endpoints and longer follow-up are warranted.

title: GG01-34: Optical versus Digital Flexible Ureteroscopy: A Prospective and Randomized Trial
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 2

speakers.organization: Santa Casa de São Paulo School of Medical Sciences

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: In the past two decades, urolithiasis prevalence has risen, affecting about 7% of women and 10.3% of men in the U. S., with annual costs around $2 billion. Flexible ureteroscopy (FU) is widely used for renal stones larger than 1 cm. A key development in this field is the digital flexible ureteroscope (DFU), featuring high-resolution cameras that replace traditional optical fibers. This enhances durability, efficiency, and reduces weight, according to manufacturers. The objective of this study is to compare the efficacy and safety of digital ureteroscopes with those of traditional optical ureteroscopes. METHODS: This randomized clinical trial involved patients with renal or proximal ureteral stones measuring 1 to 2.5 cm. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group 1 underwent the procedure using a digital flexible ureteroscope, and Group 2 was treated using a fiber-optic flexible ureteroscope, both with similar diameters and working channel sizes. Each patient underwent a preoperative CT scan and a follow-up CT 30 days post-surgery. Outcomes were classified as Stone-Free, Stones < 4 mm, or Stones \> 4 mm, with success defined by patients achieving Stone-Free or Stones < 4 mm statuses. All procedures were conducted by a senior urology resident, under experienced supervision. RESULTS: The study was conducted prospectively from March 2019 to February 2022, involving 94 patients, 43 using a digital flexible ureteroscope and 51 an optical one. Most participants were female (64%), averaging 44 years, and 59% were classified as ASA II. Preoperatively, 54% had a double J stent, and 32% had lower calyx stones, mostly hard stones over 1000 Hounsfield units. Intraoperatively, mean surgical times were similar (63 minutes for digital, 61 minutes for optical), and fluoroscopy usage time, which was also comparable, averaged 64 seconds for the digital ureteroscope and 54 seconds for the optical ureteroscope. Conversely, the optical group used significantly less saline infusion (1447 ml vs. 1627 ml, p<0.01) and had significantly superior postoperative flexion and deflection (267 degrees vs. 257 degrees for flexion, 265 degrees vs. 255 degrees for deflection, p<0.01). Postoperative CT analysis revealed no statistically significant differences in failure rates between the two techniques. Digital ureteroscopes experienced a 27.3% failure rate, compared to a 33.3% failure rate with optical ureteroscopes (p=0.592). Complication rates were 9.8% for optical and 7.3% for digital ureteroscopes (p=0.906). All complications were Clavien-Dindo grade I, minor adverse events not requiring further surgical or therapeutic intervention. CONCLUSIONS: Digital ureteroscopes did not demonstrate superiority in stone-free rates or complications. Both technologies remain safe and effective options for the treatment of renal stones.

title: GG01-35: Prevalence Of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms In Patients With Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1
parentSessionTitle: Global Gateway Posters Day 1
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1, Steinert disease) is the most common hereditary muscular dystrophy in adults, with a prevalence of 4.7–15.2 per 100,000. This autosomal dominant, multisystem disorder causes myotonia, distal muscle atrophy, cataracts, endocrine dysfunction, infertility, cognitive impairment, and cardiac conduction defects. Despite DM1’s diverse manifestations, data on lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) remain scarce. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included consecutive DM1 patients aged≥18 years, evaluated at a specialized neuromuscular clinic. Muscular impairment was graded using the Muscular Impairment Rating Scale (grades 1–5), and functional status was measured with the Modified Barthel Index. LUTS were assessed in men with the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) and in women using ICIQ-FLUTS. A symptomatic patient was defined as IPSS≥8 or similar cutoff for females. Overactive bladder (OAB) was evaluated via ICIQ-OAB, and urinary incontinence (UI) with the ICIQ-UI SF. Bowel function was examined using the Neurogenic Bowel Dysfunction Score (NBDS), and quality of life (QoL) via WHOQOL-BREF. RESULTS: 36 patients (median age 43 years, IQR 21–73; 50% male) were included. Muscular impairment was moderate, with 38.9% with MIRS grade 2, 41.6% with grade 3, and 19.5% with grade 4\. As for functionality, 15 (41.7%) had moderate to complete dependence and only 10 (27.8%) were fully independent. The overall prevalence of LUTS was 75% (66.6% in men, 83.3% in women). Storage symptoms were most common (68.8%), with voiding symptoms in 22.2% and post-micturition in 13.9%. Moderate to severe LUTS occurred in 22.3% of men and 38.8% of women. OAB was diagnosed in 27.8% of men and 55.6% of women. UI affected 58.3% overall (50% of men, 66.7% of women). Moderate to severe bowel dysfunction was observed in 13.8%. Most patients (61%) reported being satisfied with their QoL. Higher Barthel Index scores correlated with lower prevalence of LUTS (p=0.025) and urinary incontinence (p=0.005), indicating that greater functional independence predicted fewer LUTS. CONCLUSIONS: LUTS, mainly storage-related and urgency urinary incontinence, are highly prevalent in DM1, affecting men and women similarly. Greater functional independence is associated with a reduced burden of LUTS and urinary incontinence in DM1 patients. | | | --- | | |

title: GG01-36: Financial Literacy among Graduating Canadian Urology Residents Compared to Faculty
