CONCLUSIONS: On population screening data, AI-DSS achieved equivalent or superior detection of clinically significant prostate cancer compared with MRI/PSA pathways whilst reducing biopsy rates and overdiagnosis. The benefit was greatest for screening pathways using upfront MRI without a PSA threshold or following PSA≥1. The small dataset and low number of events is a limitation. | | | --- | | |

title: IP04-22: Performance of a Large Language Model in Predicting Clinical Management for New Prostate Cancer and Kidney Stone Visits
parentSessionTitle: IP04: Surgical Technology & Simulation: Artificial Intelligence
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Electronic medical record platforms are developing proprietary artificial intelligence (AI) tools to enhance clinical decision making, such as Epic’s advanced reasoning tool. However, limited research has evaluated the accuracy of existing, publicly available large language models (LLMs) within urology. This study assessed the ability of GPT-5 to predict appropriate next steps in clinical management for new patients evaluated for prostate cancer or kidney stones at Johns Hopkins Hospital. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed new patient clinic visits for a provider specializing in prostate cancer and one in kidney stones. Basic demographic data, past medical and surgical histories, relevant laboratory values, and relevant imaging reports were extracted for all visits. For 10 prostate cancer visits, biopsy findings available at the time of the appointment were included. For 10 kidney stone visits, prior stone histories were extracted. These variables were entered into a HIPAA-secured version of GPT-5 using a standardized prompt to generate next-step management recommendations. Each response was independently evaluated by a senior urology resident, blinded to data extraction, and graded for accuracy on a 5-point Likert scale (1=inaccurate, 5=fully accurate) relative to the provider’s documented clinical plan. Descriptive statistics summarized accuracy scores, and a Mann-Whitney U test compared mean accuracy between visit types. RESULTS: Across 20 new patient visits, GPT-5-generated clinical recommendations achieved high accuracy (median 5 \[interquartile range 4-5\]). Accuracy was comparable between prostate cancer and kidney stone visits (mean 4.2 ± 0.92 vs 4.7 ± 0.48; p=0.76). The LLM received a perfect score for a prostate cancer visit where it appropriately recommended deferring biopsy given a negative MRI and low malignancy risk. Minor discrepancies involved suggesting follow-up digital rectal exams or laboratory tests not discussed by the clinician. For kidney stone visits, most deductions stemmed from minor medication adjustments or screening recommendations tangentially related to the presenting concern. CONCLUSIONS: LLMs can generate accurate and contextually appropriate management recommendations for new urology patients using pre-visit data. Performance was particularly strong for kidney stone evaluations and remained high even in prostate cancer cases that typically require nuanced, patient-directed decision making. Remaining inaccuracies largely involved unnecessary testing or minor screening recommendations, which may be reduced through targeted prompt refinement and broader variable collection.

title: IP04-23: Can AI Judge Urodynamic Study Quality? Validation Using the Bristol UTraQ Scale
parentSessionTitle: IP04: Surgical Technology & Simulation: Artificial Intelligence

speakers.organization: Faculdade de Medicina da Universidade do Porto

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Urodynamic studies (UDS) are essential tools for evaluating lower urinary tract dysfunction, but the reliability of the decisions based on them depends critically on the technical quality of the recordings. The Bristol Urodynamic Trace Quality (UTraQ) scale was developed to provide a framework for assessing the technical adequacy of UDS. Artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models (LLMs) have recently become widely available and have shown potential across several areas of healthcare. While their performance in interpreting UDS remains limited, given the complexity of waveform analysis, quality assessment mainly relies on written or structural information, potentially making it a more suitable application for these models. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of an LLM (ChatGPT) in applying the Bristol UTraQ scale, and to compare its scoring with that of an expert. METHODS: The 50 most recent UDS performed at our centre, up to 30 September 2025, were included from patients who consented to participate. For each examination, anonymised images of the filling and pressure-flow phases were submitted to ChatGPT (version 5) using a structured prompt to answer all 24 UTraQ items. All AI outputs were automatically stored in a database. An experienced urodynamicist, blinded to the AI results, independently scored the same studies. Only comparable items (excluding 999) were analysed, and percentage agreement and Cohen's κ were calculated globally and by domain (pre-filling, filling, voiding). RESULTS: Fifty UDS were analysed. According to the expert, the median UTRAQ score was 77.8% (IQR 72.2–80.0%), indicating overall acceptable but suboptimal technical quality. The most frequent deficiencies were patient position not indicated (item 11: 19/49 studies), missing start/end of voiding markers (item 20: 48/48), and absence of the Qmax marker (item 22: 48/48). Pre-filling items were almost universally satisfactory. A total of 863 comparable item pairs were evaluated. The overall agreement between ChatGPT and the expert was 90.5%, with a Cohen's κ of 0.74 (substantial). Agreement was highest in the pre-filling domain (97.7%; κ=0.91), high but asymmetric in the filling domain (88.8%; κ=0.09), and lower in the voiding domain (82.5%; κ=0.65), largely reflecting systematic absence of voiding markers. CONCLUSIONS: ChatGPT applied the Bristol UTraQ scale with high agreement to an expert urodynamicist, demonstrating strong reproducibility in structured technical evaluation. As UTRAQ scoring relies primarily on identifiable written or symbolic elements rather than waveform interpretation, LLMs appear reliable to support this task. AI-assisted quality assessment may provide a fast, standardised, and objective approach for audit and training in urodynamics. Future developments combining textual and signal-based analysis could further advance automated urodynamic quality control.

title: IP04-24: Real-Time AI-Based Smoke Removal in Laparoscopic Surgery: First In-Vivo Feasibility Study
parentSessionTitle: IP04: Surgical Technology & Simulation: Artificial Intelligence

speakers.organization: Mount Sinai Icahn School of Medicine

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Visual clarity is essential for safety and efficiency in minimally invasive surgery (MIS). However, surgical smoke generated by electrocautery often obstructs the operative field, contributing to interruptions, prolonged procedure time, and increased risk of complications. While artificial intelligence (AI)-based smoke removal methods have shown promise in offline analyses, real-time clinical application has not yet been demonstrated. This study presents the first documented in-vivo demonstration of real-time AI-powered smoke removal during laparoscopic surgery, using a system called CLARIS by vopemed. METHODS: In August 2025, a feasibility session was performed in a live porcine model undergoing laparoscopic nephrectomy. Surgical smoke was generated via monopolar electrocautery, with trocar valves closed to create dense smoke conditions. The laparoscopic video signal was routed through the CLARIS console, which processed the feed and displayed the desmoked image to the surgeon. Frames were retrospectively analyzed using Dark Channel Prior (DCP) and Fog Aware Density Evaluator (FADE), two referenceless smoke metrics. Higher values indicate greater smoke density. RESULTS: CLARIS operated continuously with no interruptions or frame instability for 30 minutes, processing a total of 18,139 frames at 1080p and 20 fps. The original video feed showed an average DCP of 1.25 ± 0.35 and average FADE of 61.47 ± 20.73, which improved by 12.8% and 31.2%, respectively, following CLARIS processing (1.09 ± 0.33 and 42.32 ± 15.98). The operating surgeon qualitatively reported improved visibility during smoke events, noting clearer tissue contrast and more defined anatomic structures, such as kidney edges. Dissection could be performed without interruption for smoke evacuation. No adverse events occurred, and integration required no workflow modifications. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the first in-vivo application of real-time AI-based smoke removal during laparoscopic surgery. CLARIS integrated into the existing technical stack, maintained stable operation, did not disrupt workflow, and improved contrast by removing smoke. Future work will improve the model's performance and validate it across multiple surgeons, procedures, and setups to assess generalizability and clinical impact.

title: IP04-25: KTGrow-ML: A Novel, Machine-Learning-Based, Model To Predict The Future Growth Of Kidney Tumors
parentSessionTitle: IP04: Surgical Technology & Simulation: Artificial Intelligence
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The detection of small kidney tumors has risen dramatically and often presents a diagnostic and management dilemma due to their heterogenous biology. Estimating future kidney tumor growth could enable more personalized management by reducing unnecessary interventions for indolent lesions and optimizing active surveillance frequency. The objective of this study was to develop and evaluate KTGrow-ML, a machine-learning (ML)-based prediction model to estimate the future growth of a kidney tumor. METHODS: We used electronic health record data from a large healthcare network to identify patients with serial size measurements for a suspicious kidney tumor or complex kidney cyst in radiology reports between 2011 and 2025. Tumor characteristics were extracted using our previously validated large language model (LLM)-based approach. The dataset was randomly split into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. Supervised ML models were developed to predict tumor size at 6 and 12 months and compared against two baselines: recent-slope extrapolation and per-patient linear trend. Model performance was assessed using root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and R2. Feature importance was evaluated using SHAP values. RESULTS: We identified 496,732 radiology reports with potential descriptions of a kidney tumor. Of these, the LLM classified 46,334 as having a kidney tumor with size dimensions. After applying inclusion criteria, 19,059 reports from 6,550 unique patients were analyzed. Median age was 68.6 (interquartile range (IQR) 58.9-76.8), 43.5% were female, and median tumor size was 2.20 cm (IQR 1.50-3.60). All ML models significantly outperformed both baselines for 6- and 12-month predictions (Figure 1, p0.05). The best-performing model, Elastic Net regression (KTGrow-ML), achieved a 6-month RMSE of 1.14 (95% CI 0.41–1.16), MAE 0.54 (0.25–0.56), and R2 0.77 (0.76–0.95); and a 12-month RMSE of 1.14 (0.60–2.39), MAE 0.51 (0.47–1.31), and R2 0.61 (−2.93–0.89). Current tumor size was the most influential predictor followed by size at diagnosis. CONCLUSIONS: We developed KTGrow-ML, a novel ML model to predict the future growth of kidney tumors. Our model significantly outperforms baselines and if further validated, could be used to reduce overtreatment of indolent tumors and personalize active surveillance schedules.

title: IP04-26: Towards Clinical Translation of a Real-time, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Assisted Cystoscopy System for Bladder Cancer Detection
parentSessionTitle: IP04: Surgical Technology & Simulation: Artificial Intelligence
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: White light cystoscopy is the cornerstone of bladder cancer detection and surveillance; however, challenges remain, including identification of carcinoma in situ, multifocal tumors, and distinguishing cancerous and benign lesions. Computer-vision artificial intelligence (AI) models for tumor detection have strong potential to overcome these limitations. This study aims to address the clinical translation hurdles related to workflow compatibility and usability by integrating an AI-assisted cystoscopy system in clinical settings. METHODS: We developed an end-to-end AI-assisted cystoscopy system featuring a compact, custom-built video processing hub measuring 377 mm × 330 mm × 82 mm ( Fig. 1) and an intuitive graphical user interface for integration with standard endoscopy towers. The hub supports up to four HDMI connections, enabling real-time switching between various video inputs via a front-panel control. Equipped with an NVIDIA RTX 5060 graphics card, the system provides real-time AI inference displayed as toggleable, low-latency overlays. A foot pedal allows the operator to quickly cycle through or deactivate AI overlays. For procedural safety, a hardware bypass button ensures the primary video feed remains uninterrupted in the event of a system error. A 14-question usability survey was designed to assess clinician user experience, focusing on interface usability and utility ( Fig. 2). RESULTS: The platform was successfully deployed in 4 operating room and 3 clinic cystoscopy procedures. Survey feedback from 4 physician users confirmed the system was user-friendly and minimally disruptive to workflow. Reported limitations include noticeable system latency during transurethral resection and false positive detections of non-cancerous lesions, such as resection beds. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study demonstrates a feasible, user-centric platform for integrating AI into cystoscopy. Future efforts will focus on optimizing latency and gathering broader clinician feedback across diverse clinical settings.

title: IP04-27: Development and internal validation of machine-learning models to predict adverse pathological features in upper tract urothelial carcinoma using data from the ROBUUST 3.0 collaborative
parentSessionTitle: IP04: Surgical Technology & Simulation: Artificial Intelligence
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Reliable preoperative identification of adverse pathological features in upper tract urothelial carcinoma remains challenging and upstaging on final pathology occurs in up to 60% of patients. Current guidelines differ in preoperative risk stratification, and most established risk factors are mainly based on postoperative findings. We aimed to develop and internally validate machine-learning (ML) models for preoperative prediction of muscle-invasive (≥pT2) and node positive disease (pN+) in UTUC. METHODS: Patients who underwent radical nephroureterectomy or distal ureterectomy without neoadjuvant chemotherapy from the multi-institutional ROBUUST 3.0 registry were identifed. Routinely available preoperative variables, including demographics, biopsy pathology (grade, variant histology, cytology), clinical features (cT-stage, cN-stage, tumor size, hydronephrosis, multifocality, serume creatinine) were processed with missing data imputed using Hyperimpute. Four classifiers (elastic-net logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM and SVM-RBF) were optimized via five-fold cross validation and hyperparameter optimization via Optuna. A logistic meta-learner combined base models into a stacking ensemble. Performance was evaluated using area under the curve (AUC) and Brier score in an 80/20 train-validation split. RESULTS: A total of 3584 patients with extirpative surgery and 1596 patients who additionally underwent lymph-node dissection were identified. Muscle-invasive disease was present in 1979 (55.2%) of cases, and node-positive disease in 1595 (31.6%) cases. The stacking model achieved the best discrimination for pN+ prediction (AUC 0.78 \[95% CI: 0.72\ – 0.83\], Brier 0.16), while for ≥pT2 prediction random forest outperformed other single learners and the stacking ensemble (AUC 0.66 \[95% CI: 0.63 – 0.70\], Brier 0.23) ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191284.35857.1d.27#F1)). Significant predictors for pN+ disease were cT-stage, cN-stage and cytology. Significant predictors for >pT2 were cN-stage, creatinine and tumor size. CONCLUSIONS: Machine-learning models achieved robust accuracy for predicting nodal metastases but only moderate discrimination for muscle-invasive disease, underscoring the limitations of accurate preoperative primary tumor staging. External validation is needed to confirm clinical utility and inform preoperative risk-stratification and multimodal approaches to treatment.

title: IP04-28: Applying advanced prompt engineering techniques to generative artificial intelligence models for analyzing diagnostic quality in retrograde urethrogram images.
parentSessionTitle: IP04: Surgical Technology & Simulation: Artificial Intelligence

speakers.organization: Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Retrograde urethrograms (RUGs) are the main imaging method for evaluating urethral stricture disease. However, diagnostic quality varies with technical and anatomical factors, making consistent evaluation essential for patient management. Conventional artificial intelligence (AI) image analysis requires large datasets, which is costly and time intensive. Advanced prompting of generative AI models may offer a faster, data-efficient alternative. Our objective was to evaluate the effectiveness of advanced prompting in accurately assessing RUG quality. METHODS: We reviewed a random sample of 233 RUGs from 2010-2024 at a tertiary care centre. De-identified RUG images were labeled by a trained reviewer as diagnostic (good quality) or non-diagnostic (poor quality), with classifications verified by a reconstructive urologist. The labeled dataset was then used to evaluate a Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT)-4o AI model for automated RUG quality assessment. Using advanced prompting strategies like multishot, negative, and chain-of-thought prompting, we developed an internal GPT-based AI tool to classify each RUG as diagnostic or non-diagnostic with reasoning. To assess performance, 75 randomly selected RUGs were analyzed under two conditions: 1) with advanced prompting and 2) without any prompting (unprompted baseline). RESULTS: Mean age at RUG was 52.52 ± 18.50 years. Based on reviewer assessment, 164/233 (70.4%) studies were diagnostic and 69/233 (29.6%) non-diagnostic. The prompted model achieved first-pass accuracy of 53/75 (70.7%) and improved to 61/75 (81.3%) after an unguided “try again” prompt ( Table 1). False positives occurred in 12/75 (16.0%) and false negatives in 10/75 (13.3%). In contrast, the unprompted model reached 33/75 (44.0%) accuracy with 8/75 (10.7%) false positives and 34/75 (45.3%) false negatives. Advanced prompting performed well in identifying urethral kinks but occasionally misclassified images with obscured urethral length due to x-ray vignetting. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that advanced prompting improves the model’s ability to assess the diagnostic quality of RUGs, primarily by reducing false negatives. Future refinements, like a mixture-of-experts approach where specialized GPT-based agents evaluate individual quality factors and report back to a main model, can enhance accuracy and reliability. | | | --- | | |

title: IP04-29: Ambient Listening Technology in an Outpatient Urology Clinic: Impact on Provider Satisfaction and Return on Investment Metrics
parentSessionTitle: IP04: Surgical Technology & Simulation: Artificial Intelligence
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Ambient listening technology (ALT) leverages large language models (LLMs) to transcribe and structure patient–provider conversations into clinical documentation. Several vendors now provide ALT solutions for health systems. By removing extraneous information, highlighting salient points, and reorganizing dialogue, ALT can generate complete and concise notes. This may enhance the patient–provider relationship by reducing the documentation burden and improving electronic medical record (EMR) usability. We evaluated the impact of ALT implementation in an outpatient academic urology practice, focusing on clinical productivity and provider EMR use. METHODS: ALT was deployed across our institution’s (Emory Healthcare, Atlanta, GA) outpatient clinics beginning September 2023, using services from a third-party vendor (Abridge AI, Inc.). Data were collected from the Epic Systems Signal dashboard to assess provider time in the EMR and monthly charges from September 2023 through October 2024. All urology providers were included, regardless of ALT adoption status. RESULTS: By October 2024, 20 of 36 eligible providers (56%) were classified as high-volume ALT users, defined as using ALT for at least 50% of clinic notes. These providers used ALT in 72% of encounters on average. Overall, 35/36 (97%) providers trialed ALT at least once. Compared with non-users, high-volume users demonstrated reductions of 3.97 hours/month in note-writing time and 7.70 hours/month in total EMR time. Billing analysis showed a modest increase in coding level (mean 0.10 higher per month) but a substantial difference in charges: high-volume ALT users generated an additional $191 per encounter, averaging over $48,000 in increased monthly charges per user. They also produced 189.85 more relative value units per month compared with non-users. Of 36 providers surveyed, 13 responded. Among respondents, 53% agreed or strongly agreed that ALT improved productivity, and 70% reported perceived improvements in provider wellness. CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of ALT in outpatient urology clinics was associated with decreased EMR documentation time, increased clinical productivity, and higher billing-related outputs. Provider-reported benefits further suggest ALT may enhance efficiency and wellness in academic practice.

title: IP04-30: Modernization of a Historical Prostate Cancer Registry using Artificial Intelligence: A Tale of Two LLMs
parentSessionTitle: IP04: Surgical Technology & Simulation: Artificial Intelligence
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Since 1986, the Mayo Clinic Prostate Cancer Registry has followed over 30,000 men who underwent radical prostatectomy. Historically, data abstraction was performed by nurse abstractors, a labor intensive process. Recent advances in LLMs may provide an opportunity to modernize data collection, reduce human abstraction burden, and improve registry efficiency. We report the results of LLM data abstraction for surgical pathology data in the Mayo Clinic Prostate Cancer Registry. METHODS: Original unstructured surgical pathology reports were obtained for patients undergoing surgery from 2018-2022. LLM prompts for 13 pathology variables were developed, each run independently through two independent LLMs (Google Gemini Flash 1.5 and 2.0), and refined until the two LLMs achieved a >90% concordance. Consensus and individual LLM outputs were then compared to historical registry data collected by a trained and experienced nurse-abstractor. Discrepancies were adjudicated by a team of humans to determine the ground truth ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191284.35857.1d.30#F1)). Accuracy was compared using Fischer’s exact test. RESULTS: A total of 3210 patients were included. The dataset was split into training (2022, n=404), internal validation (2021, n=710), and test subsets (2018-2020, n=2096). Median consensus LLM error rate was 0.09% (IQR 0.03-0.16%), as compared to median human error rate of 2.81% (IQR 1.83-3.17%; p<0.01, (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191284.35857.1d.30#F2)). Notably, each individual LLM had a three times higher error rate compared to consensus LLM (Gemini 1.5 0.27% (IQR 0.09–0.34%), Gemini 2.0 0.30% (IQR 0.17%-0.48%)). Total estimated time for human data abstraction for all 13 variables in the entire cohort was 294 hours, as compared to 9 hours for our LLM pipeline. CONCLUSIONS: LLM data abstraction employing a consensus vote across two LLM models consistently yielded higher accuracy than human or single LLM abstraction alone. A dual LLM architecture holds promise in improving data abstraction efficiency and reducing errors, and should be considered for integration into all prospectively maintained longitudinal clinical registries.

title: IP05-01: Higher CONUT (Controlling for Nutritional Status) Scores are Associated with Complications After Radical Nephrectomy but Not Oncologic Outcomes
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) scores assess the nutritional-immune status of patients using albumin, cholesterol, and lymphocyte. Prior studies of patients undergoing radical nephrectomy (RN) for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) found that patients with high CONUT scores have worse overall survival (OS), cancer specific survival (CSS), and progression free survival (PFS), though these studies lacked comprehensive risk adjustment in their models. Further, no studies have examined the CONUT’s relationship with RN complications. Here, we examine the CONUT’s association with oncologic outcomes and 90 day complications after RN. METHODS: We queried our prospectively maintained nephrectomy registry for patients undergoing RN for RCC with available CONUT data. Kaplan Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression were performed for OS, CSS, and PFS for patients with clear cell RCC who had Mayo PFS and CSS scores. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression evaluated CONUT’s association with 90 day any and high grade complications. RESULTS: Among 486 patients (median follow up 7.3 years), 167 patients (34%) had a CONUT score of ≥3 (immune-nutritional depleted). Patients with high CONUT scores had higher Mayo PFS scores compared to those with low CONUT scores (8.0 vs 6.0, p<0.001). On univariable analysis, CONUT scores ≥3 were associated with worse OS (HR 1.8), CSS (HR 2.7), and PFS (HR 1.6), p<0.05 ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191288.32814.7d.01#F1), Table 1). After adjusting for Mayo PFS and CSS scores, higher CONUT scores were not associated with worse OS, CSS, and PFS. For any and high 90 day complications, a CONUT score of ≥3 was associated with more any (OR 2.2) and high grade (OR 2.4) 90 day complications on univariable analysis. This was maintained on multivariable analysis for any 90 day complications (OR 1.8, 95% CI 1.1-3.1, p=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: While patients with high CONUT scores were more likely to have aggressive disease and experience complications after RN, they were not more likely to experience oncologic events after adjusting for Mayo PFS and CSS scores, suggesting that the prior literature demonstrating this effect may be suffering from incomplete risk adjustment.

title: IP05-02: Radiomic Tumor Contact Surface Area Predicts Post-Operative Complications and Local Recurrence Outcomes for Patients Undergoing Multifocal Partial Nephrectomy
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The management of multifocal synchronous renal masses with partial nephrectomy (PNx) is a rare scenario, with sparse data to inform complication and local recurrence risk. We previously developed an Artificial Intelligence (AI) tumor segmentation model that distinguishes kidney tumor from normal renal parenchyma and quantifies several radiomics measurements. Herein, we evaluate clinical and radiomic variables associated with post-operative complications and oncologic outcomes for patients receiving multifocal PNx. METHODS: Patients who underwent planned multifocal unilateral or bilateral PNx between 2000-2024 were queried from a prospective nephrectomy registry. Our AI algorithm used contrast-enhanced CT imaging to measure tumor contact surface area (CSA), endophycity, and centricity ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191288.32814.7d.02#F1)). CSA was quantified cumulatively and by CSA of largest renal mass. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression analysis evaluated factors associated with 30-day post-operative complications and local recurrence free survival (LRFS), respectively. RESULTS: Of 155 patients, 66 underwent bilateral PNx and 89 underwent multifocal unilateral PNx with median 2 tumors removed (IQR 2-3) and median tumor size 2.6 cm (IQR 1.6-3.9). After adjusting for number of tumors and unilateral vs bilateral PNx, cumulative CSA was associated with 30-day complications (OR 1.07 per 1000 voxels, 95% CI 1.02-1.12, p=0.007, (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191288.32814.7d.02#F2)). After adjusting for unilateral vs bilateral PNx, both cumulative CSA (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.03-1.11, p=0.001) and CSA of largest renal mass (HR 1.08, 95% CI 1.02-1.15, p=0.007) were associated with LRFS with median follow up 9.5 years (IQR 6.3-12.8). Endophycity and centricity were not associated with complications or LRFS. CONCLUSIONS: Cumulative CSA was associated with 30 day post-operative complications, and both cumulative CSA and CSA of largest mass were associated with local recurrence. This AI tool may have potential applications for patient selection, surgical planning, and risk stratification for post-operative complications and oncologic outcomes among patients planned for complex PNx.

title: IP05-03: Robotic Partial Nephrectomy Defines a New Standard for Safety and Recovery: A Comprehensive Analysis of 1,441 Cases Across Three Surgical Approaches
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I

speakers.jobTitle: Urologic surgeon and clinical researcher at Sheba Medical Center and Tel Aviv University.

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To comprehensively compare clinical outcomes and define the safest, most effective standard of care, we analyzed 1,441 partial nephrectomies (PN) performed via robotic (RAPN), laparoscopic (LPN), and open (OPN) approaches at a single tertiary center. METHODS: A retrospective review of 1,441 consecutive PNs (544 RAPN, 349 LPN, 548 OPN) from 2000-2025 was performed. We analyzed general recovery metrics (Length of Stay \[LOS\], same-day discharge, transfusion rates) across the entire cohort. To ensure a valid comparison and neutralize historical selection bias, a primary complication analysis (Urine Leak \[UL\] and Renal Artery Pseudoaneurysm \[RAP\]) was performed on a core, modern sub-cohort of 785 patients (2012-2022). This sub-cohort was confirmed to have no significant difference in baseline RENAL nephrometry scores across all three arms (p=0.55). Multivariable logisticregression (MVA) was used to identify independent predictors for major complications. RESULTS: Analysis of the full cohort (N=1,441) demonstrated clear advantages for RAPN in recovery metrics. The median length of stay for RAPN was 2.9 days, markedly shorter than 7.24 for LPN and 8.04 for OPN (p<0.001), with 25% of RAPN patients eligible for same-day discharge (vs. <5% for LPN/OPN). Blood transfusion rates were also significantly lower for RAPN (3.2%) compared to LPN (10.6%) and OPN (14.4%) (p<0.001). In the modern, complexity-matched cohort (N=785), RAPN demonstrated superior safety. The overall Urine Leak (UL) incidence was 2.4%, but the rate for RAPN was substantially lower at 0.75% (vs. 3.7% OPN, 4.91% LPN; p=0.03). Similarly, the Pseudoaneurysm (RAP) incidence was 2.1% overall, with RAPN again showing the lowest rate at 1.0% (vs. 3.4% OPN, 3.3% LPN; p=0.04). On Multivariable Analysis (MVA), the surgical approach emerged as a powerful, independent predictor for both complications. Compared to RAPN as the reference, both LPN (OR 6.8, p=0.007) and OPN (OR 5.2, p=0.014) independently predicted higher UL rates. The LPN/OPN approaches, along with operative time, were also the only independent predictors for RAP (p<0.05). While median operative time was longer for RAPN (169 min) vs. LPN (122 min), one-year eGFR preservation was similar across all groups (p=0.53). CONCLUSIONS: In this large-scale comparative analysis, RAPN demonstrates superior perioperative recovery (shorter LOS, fewer transfusions) and superior safety (significantly lower rates of UL and RAP). After rigorously adjusting for confounders in a modern cohort with comparable tumor complexity, RAPN remains an independent protective factor against major complications. These data reinforce RAPN as the standard of care for nephron-sparing surgery.

title: IP05-04: Nephrometry Scores as Predictors of Trifecta, Pentafecta, and Postoperative Renal Function Following Robotic Partial Nephrectomy
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the utility of tumor size, RENAL, PADUA, and SPARE Nephrometry Scores (NSs) in predicting the likelihood of achieving trifecta and pentafecta outcomes, as well as the risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) and kidney disease progression at 12 months following RAPN. METHODS: Retrospective review was performed on IRB-approved, prospectively maintained database to identify 1787 consecutive cases of primary, non-metastatic small renal masses who underwent RAPN between 2011 and 2024. All pre-operative radiological images were reviewed by a single resident physician, who characterized all tumors based on the NSs. Trifecta outcome was defined as cases with warm ischemia time <25 minutes, negative surgical margin, and absence of complications. Pentafecta included the trifecta outcomes with the addition of >90% renal function preservation and absence of kidney disease progression at 12 months. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were completed to determine the predictive ability for the tumor size and each of the NS. RESULTS: Trifecta and pentafecta were achieved in 52.7% and 22.2%, respectively. All three NSs were established as statistically significant predictors of trifecta, pentafecta, and postoperative AKI, with all demonstrating comparable yet limited predictive performance (AUC 0.573–0.645). Notably, tumor diameter (AUC 0.649–0.665) was shown to outperform the NSs in predicting the likelihood of achieving trifecta and pentafecta, as well as the risk of AKI. None of the scoring systems were identified as independent predictors of kidney disease progression at 12 months. CONCLUSIONS: Although lower RENAL, PADUA, and SPARE NSs were significantly associated with achieving surgical success and reduced risk of AKI, their predictive performance was modest and consistently outperformed by a simpler and more objective measure, such as tumor diameter. Future studies remain necessary to re-evaluate the broader clinical utility of NS in predicting surgical and functional outcomes, in addition to its original purpose as standardized tools for the anatomical characterization of renal tumors.

title: IP05-05: Machine Learning–Based Predictive Model for Trifecta Achievement in Robot-Assisted Partial Nephrectomy
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and internally validate a machine learning-based nomogram for predicting trifecta achievement in patients undergoing robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN). METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included patients who underwent RAPN between 2011 and 2025 at a tertiary academic hospital. Trifecta was defined as the presence of negative surgical margins, warm ischemia time ≤25 minutes, and absence of perioperative complications in the same patient. Preoperative and intraoperative variables were selected based on the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression. Selected predictors were incorporated into a multivariable logistic regression model to construct a nomogram. Decision curve analysis (DCA) and area under the curve (AUC) were calculated to evaluate the model performance. RESULTS: Among 426 patients included, trifecta was achieved in 87.7%. Of the 15 perioperative variables initially evaluated with LASSO, five were retained as significant predictors. In multivariable logistic regression, trifecta failure was independently associated with longer operative time (OR 1.014, 95% CI 1.008–1.021; p<0.001), higher blood loss (OR 1.002, 95% CI 1.001–1.003; p<0.001), entry into the collecting system (OR 4.151, 95% CI 2.237–7.702; p<0.001), and perioperative blood transfusion (OR 24.226, 95% CI 7.385–79.477; p<0.001). On the other hand, posterior tumor location was in favor of trifecta achievement (OR 0.435, 95% CI 0.206–0.919; p=0.029). The model demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.792, 95% CI 0.738–0.845), acceptable calibration (bootstrap-corrected slope 0.91, intercept 0.13), and DCA indicated higher net benefit than treat-all/none strategies for thresholds of 0.10–0.75. CONCLUSIONS: This LASSO-guided, clinically interpretable nomogram predicts trifecta achievement after RAPN with strong internal validity. Given the association between trifecta status and favorable long-term renal and oncologic outcomes, this tool can support perioperative risk assessment, surgical planning, and patient counseling.

title: IP05-06: Personalized Predictors Of Renal Recovery After Partial Nephrectomy
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Renal function recovery after partial nephrectomy (PN) results from a multifaceted interplay of modifiable and non-modifiable factors such as amount of spared parenchyma, ischemia duration, patient comorbidities, renal anatomy, and surgical approach. We aimed to delineate the non-linear relationship between ischemia time and renal function recovery, and to identify subgroups more vulnerable to ischemic injury. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 491 patients who underwent PN at a tertiary referral center. Renal function was assessed preoperatively and at 12 months after surgery, and the relative variation in estimated glomerular filtration rate (ΔeGFR%) was computed. Locally weighted scatterplot smoothing (LOWESS) curves were applied to explore non-linear trends between ischemia time and postoperative ΔeGFR across clinical and surgical subgroups. RESULTS: Median age was 61 years (IQR: 52–69), and 68% were male. Hypertension (48%) and diabetes mellitus (10%) were the most frequent comorbidities, while 2.2% of patients had a solitary kidney. Median ischemia time was 17 minutes (IQR 13–22). At 1 year, the median ΔeGFR was –6.5% (IQR –16 to -0.15). As illustrated in the LOWESS analyses, patients with hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, or a solitary kidney exhibited a steep decline in renal function beyond 20 minutes of ischemia, whereas those without such comorbidities showed a flatter curve, suggesting greater tolerance to ischemic insult. Tumour location and surgical approach had negligible influence: both subgroups displayed a stable ΔeGFR% for ischemia durations below 20 minutes, followed by a steeper decline thereafter, particularly among patients with non-inferior pole tumours or those undergoing open surgery. CONCLUSIONS: Renal function recovery after PN is shaped by a nuanced interaction between ischemia time, surgical technique, and patient comorbidities. Recognizing the unique sensitivity of hypertensive, dyslipidemic, and solitary-kidney patients can guide personalized surgical planning and postoperative monitoring. Integrating patient-specific risk profiles with surgical metrics may optimize functional preservation and long-term renal outcomes.

title: IP05-07: Short- and Long-term Functional Outcomes in a Large Cohort of PN Patients Managed with Prolonged Ischemia
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Previous studies suggest irreversible renal functional decline begins after 25-30 minutes of clamp time during partial nephrectomy (PN), and hypothermia is protective. We aimed to provide a more robust analysis of functional recovery after prolonged warm ischemia (WI), including quantification of short- and long-term effects. METHODS: 568 PN patients at our center (2011-2020) with prolonged ischemia (>30minutes) with necessary data were evaluated. Recovery from ischemia (Recischemia) was defined as ipsilateral GFR preserved normalized by parenchymal volume preserved, and would be 100% if all nephrons recovered completely from ischemia. The impact of prolonged ischemia on Recischemia, spectrum-score (analogous to AKI), and percent annual decline of ipsilateral GFR and parenchymal volume were assessed. RESULTS: Median tumor size and R. E. N. A. L were 4.3 cm and 8, respectively. The prolonged ischemia cohorts included patients managed with hypothermia (n=268) and WI (n=300). Median ischemia times for the hypothermia and WI cohorts were 42 and 35 minutes, respectively. Median Recischemia for cold versus WI was 96% and 85%, respectively (Table 1, (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191288.32814.7d.07#F1), p<0.01). Recischemia fell ≈9% for each additional 10 min of prolonged WI beyond 30 minutes. Increased spectrum score was seen with prolonged ischemia, whether cold or warm. GFR at 3 years was generally stable at 95% and 97% preserved, respectively, in both the cold and warm cohorts, and substantial atrophy was not seen ( (https://www.auajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1097/01.JU.0001191288.32814.7d.07#F1)). On multivariable analysis, prolonged WI and increased spectrum score were associated with reduced Recischemia (both p<0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Our results confirm the significant negative impact of prolonged warm ischemia on functional recovery during clamped PN, and hypothermia proved to be protective. Early ipsilateral renal dysfunction was mostly dependent on ischemia time, whether cold or warm. Long-term function and parenchymal volume generally remained stable despite exposure to prolonged ischemia. Prolonged warm ischemia should be avoided in patients with solitary kidneys and/or moderate-severe preexisting CKD. NA.

title: IP05-08: Impact of Prolonged Warm Ischemia during Clamped Partial Nephrectomy: Comparison between Japanese and American Cohorts
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I

speakers.organization: Department Of Urology, Tokyo Women's Medical University

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Introduction: Recent research suggests that functional recovery begins to decline after ≈30 minutes of warm-ischemia-time (WIT) following clamped partial-nephrectomy (PN). However, the extent of this decline and populations at risk remain unclear. Our objective was to identify factors associated with functional decline following prolonged WIT in Japanese and American patients. METHODS: Methods: A multi-institutional retrospective-review of PN patients managed with prolonged WIT(>30minutes) at Tokyo Women’s and Cleveland Clinic(2010-2024). Inclusion required pre and post-operative serum-creatinine and cross-sectional imaging. Ipsilateral split-renal- function(SRF) was assessed using parenchymal-volume-analysis(PVA). Recovery from ischemia(RecIschemia) was defined: ipsilateral GFR preserved normalized by percent- parenchymal-volume-preserved(PPVP). Multivariable analysis identified factors associated with RecIschemia, PPVP, and %global GFR preservation. RESULTS: Results: 300 U. S./171 Japanese patients met inclusion criteria. U. S. patients had increased comorbidities, including obesity, hypertension, and cardiovascular-disease. A significant and similar decline in global GFR for every additional 10 minutes of WIT was seen in both the Japanese and U. S. patients (3.1% vs. 4.0%, respectively, p=0.41). Independent predictors of decline in global GFR were PPVP in both cohorts and longer WIT only for U. S. patients. R. E. N. A. L. and tumor-size were primary drivers of decline in PPVP, and WIT and HTN were drivers of decline in RecIschemia, but only in U. S. patients. CONCLUSIONS: Conclusion: Japanese and U. S. patients undergoing PN with prolonged WIT experienced similar decline in global GFR, albeit driven by different factors potentially reflecting differences in patient populations and/or surgical technique. Our data suggest that avoiding prolonged WIT may be important in patients with solitary kidneys and/or severe CKD, although further studies will be needed.

title: IP05-09: 3D perfusion zone models allow for more accurate and more frequent selective arterial clamping during robot-assisted partial nephrectomy: Interim results of the multicentric randomized controlled PODRACING trial
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Although the superiority of selective clamping (SC) over main-artery clamping (MAC) in robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) remains controversial, SC may offer benefits in certain cases. Improved prediction of kidney perfusion could enhance the precision of SC and thereby promote better preservation of healthy renal tissue. PODRACING (Planning Operative strategy using a Digital Renal Artery ClampING tool) is a multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluating the benefits of 3D perfusion zone (3DPZ) models in RAPN. The trial is registered on ClinicalTrials. gov (NCT06536439) and was approved by the Belgian Federal Agency for Medicines and Health Products (CIV-23-11-044854). Herein, we present our pre-planned interim analysis of the primary endpoint and key secondary endpoint regarding clamping strategy. METHODS: Patients undergoing RAPN were randomized 1:1 to either an experimental group (CT scan \+ 3DPZ) or control group (CT scan only), stratified by PADUA complexity score, hospital, and whether SC was deemed feasible or not. The primary endpoint, performing as planned a SC strategy, was analyzed in a subgroup of patients where SC was deemed feasible. The key secondary endpoint, clamping strategy performed (SC vs MAC), was studied in the total population. Both endpoints were analyzed using a Chi-Squared (X2) test. RESULTS: In total, 107 patients underwent RAPN in 4 participating Belgian centers from July 2024 until October 2025. 27/107 cases were classified as PADUA high-risk (≥10), all other cases were PADUA 9 or lower. In 103/107 cases, SC was deemed feasible. SC was planned in 87/107 cases and performed in 73/107 cases. In 65/73 cases, SC was performed as planned. The use of a 3DPZ model was significantly associated with performing more accurate (p<0.00001) ( Table 1) and more frequent (p=0.000076) SC. CONCLUSIONS: PODRACING is the first RCT exploring the benefits of 3DPZ models in RAPN. The interim analysis of our ongoing trial shows that the use of 3DPZ models is strongly correlated with performing more accurate and more frequent SC during RAPN, and thus preserving healthier kidney tissue by less extensive ischemia. More secondary and exploratory endpoints –including renal function, surgical time and quality of life– are currently being studied. | | | --- | | |

title: IP05-10: Three-Dimensional Imaging for Perioperative Planning in Partial Nephrectomy: A Meta-Analysis of 3,485 Patients
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Partial nephrectomy (PN) remains the gold standard for localized renal masses. Optimal outcomes depend on meticulous preoperative planning and precise intraoperative navigation, which traditionally rely on two-dimensional (2D) imaging that may not fully capture renal anatomy or spatial relationships. Three-dimensional (3D) visualization modalities, including virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and 3D-printed models, offer enhanced anatomical understanding and more accurate surgical planning. This meta-analysis evaluated the impact of 3D imaging on perioperative, oncological, and functional outcomes in patients undergoing PN. METHODS: A systematic search of four databases was conducted through July 2025. Eligible studies compared 3D visualization with standard 2D imaging in adults with renal masses undergoing PN. Outcomes included warm ischemia time (WIT), operative time (OT), estimated blood loss (EBL), positive surgical margins (PSM), major complications (Clavien–Dindo≥III), postoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), length of stay (LOS), and intraoperative complications. Data were pooled using mean differences (MD) or odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Subgroup analyses were performed by surgical approach. RESULTS: Twenty-three studies (2 RCTs, 6 prospective, 15 retrospective) with 3,485 patients met inclusion criteria. Baseline characteristics were comparable, 3D imaging significantly reduced PSM rates (OR=0.56, p=0.001), decreased EBL (MD=–25.07 ml, p=0.01), lowered major complication rates (OR=0.60, p=0.02), improved postoperative eGFR (MD=2.0, p=0.02), and shortened hospital stay (MD=–0.64 days, p=0.03). Subgroup analyses revealed consistent trends favoring 3D visualization across surgical approaches. The laparoscopic subgroup showed the greatest benefit, with significant reductions in EBL, WIT, OT and PSM, while in robotic procedures, 3D visualization significantly improved postoperative eGFR. CONCLUSIONS: The use of 3D imaging was associated with improved surgical and functional outcomes, including positive surgical margins, fewer postoperative complications, reduced blood loss, shorter hospital stay, and better renal function preservation. Future randomized studies are warranted to assess cost-effectiveness and long-term functional outcomes.

title: IP05-11: Seeing is Deciding: Virtual 3D Models Improve Decisional Quality in Renal Mass Counseling
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Treatment decisions for small renal masses (SRMs) remain variable despite comparable oncologic outcomes across options, suggesting that patient comprehension during counseling influences treatment selection. Virtual 3D models provide an interactive visual aid to improve understanding of anatomy and treatment trade-offs. We evaluated whether incorporating patient-specific 3D kidney models during consultation improves decisional quality compared to a historical control cohort. METHODS: We conducted a prospective pilot study of 20 patients counseled for SRMs using interactive virtual 3D models generated from CT/MRI via a cloud-based segmentation platform, compared with a historical control cohort (n=73) from Shirk et al., 2018. After consultation, patients completed validated surveys: Decisional Conflict Scale (DCS; total and subscales), kidney cancer knowledge assessment (9-item), and Service Satisfaction Scale for Cancer Care (SSS-CC). Surveys were administered immediately post-consultation. Group comparisons used Wilcoxon rank-sum and chi-square tests. RESULTS: Among 93 patients (20 3D vs 73 controls), groups were similar in age, sex, and race. Patients counseled with 3D models had lower decisional conflict on the Informed subscale (median 0.0 \[IQR 0–8.3\] vs 16.7 \[0–33.3\]; p=0.014). No differences were seen in total DCS, other subscales, or satisfaction. High knowledge scores were more common in the 3D group (80% vs 63%; p=0.15). Post-consultation treatment choice differed: patients receiving 3D models more often selected active surveillance (40% vs 11%; p=0.005) ( Table 1). CONCLUSIONS: Virtual 3D models reduced decisional conflict in the informed subscale and influenced treatment choice toward active surveillance, even when measured immediately post-consult. These findings suggest that visualizing tumor anatomy enhances comprehension and promotes preference-concordant decision-making. Continued accrual will refine these estimates and assess durability of effects across a larger cohort.

title: IP05-12: Application of Real-time Digital Twin Navigation and Warning System Based on Deep Learning and Augmented Reality Technology Platform (AI+AR) in Robot-assisted and Laparoscopic Partial Nephrectomy (NCT07020169)
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Minimally invasive (robot-assisted and laparoscopic) partial nephrectomy is the mainstream surgical approach for treating T1a and some T1b stage renal tumors. Urologists aim for tumor control, low complication rates, and renal function preservation in this procedure. Complete tumor resection at an appropriate distance from the tumor capsule ensures tumor control and renal function preservation. Identifying important vessels (arteries, veins, and collecting system) during resection is crucial for reducing intraoperative and postoperative complications. Additionally, for endophytic tumors, their hidden location makes intraoperative identification difficult. This project aims to use artificial intelligence (AI) deep learning to construct a three-dimensional vascular model of the kidney and, through augmented reality (AR) technology, establish a real-time, field-of-view-following digital twin navigation and warning system in minimally invasive partial nephrectomy to plan the resection range in real time and warn of potential damage to important vessels. METHODS: The clinical trial registration number of this project is NCT07020169. Patients with T1a and some T1b stage single renal tumors (with normal contralateral renal function) scheduled for minimally invasive partial nephrectomy at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from March 2024 to the present were included. Patients with anatomically or functionally solitary kidneys and angiomyolipomas were excluded. All patients underwent 64-slice enhanced CT (pixel size 0.47-0.74 mm/pixel, slice thickness 0.5 mm) before surgery. CT DICOM data were imported into a self-developed AI convolutional neural network segmentation algorithm (Meta Grayscale Adaptive, MGA) to automatically segment and construct a three-dimensional model including the kidney, tumor, and vessels (arteries, veins, renal pelvis and calyces). Real-time digital twins were constructed using vector point marking and real-time camera pose transformation algorithms and superimposed onto the robot-assisted or laparoscopic surgical field for navigation and warning. Three experienced urologic surgeons performed minimally invasive partial nephrectomy using the real-time digital twin navigation and warning system. Patient and tumor basic information, perioperative data were recorded, and the intraoperative digital twin matching degree was evaluated using the Dice score, and the doctor's acceptance was evaluated using the Likert scale. RESULTS: All 112 patients (67 robot-assisted and 45 laparoscopic) successfully completed the surgery without conversion to open or radical resection. The average tumor diameter was 3.1 cm, with a median RENAL score of 7 points, including 14 cases of completely endophytic tumors. The average operation time was 98 minutes, and the average warm ischemia time was 22 minutes. After analyzing 11,200 frames of images, the average Dice score for the kidney contour was 0.86, and for the tumor was 0.82. The average Likert score for robot-assisted surgery was 8.6 points, and for laparoscopic surgery was 8.1 points. Only one patient had postoperative bleeding requiring interventional treatment. CONCLUSIONS: The digital twin navigation and warning system based on AI+AR is safe and reliable in minimally invasive partial nephrectomy. This system has high matching accuracy and robustness, which helps in tumor boundary identification and reduces the risk of surgical complications.

title: IP05-13: Three-Dimensional Image-Guided Robot-Assisted Partial Nephrectomy for Tumors in Horseshoe Kidneys: A European Multicentre Case Series (YAU RCC – UroCCR)
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Renal tumors arising in horseshoe kidneys (HSKs) pose major surgical challenges due to complex vascular anatomy, limited mobility, and proximity to critical structures. Three-dimensional (3D) modeling can improve anatomical understanding and support tailored ischemia strategies. This European multicentre study reports outcomes of 3D image-guided robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) for tumors in HSKs. METHODS: Patients with HSK tumors treated with RAPN using patient-specific 3D reconstructions were included. Virtual models from multiphase CT scans detailed renal vasculature, collecting system, and tumor–parenchyma interface. Reconstructions supported preoperative planning and intraoperative cognitive guidance displayed on the robotic console. Clinical, anatomical, perioperative, functional, and oncological outcomes were retrospectively analyzed across European tertiary centres. RESULTS: Twenty-four patients were included (83% male; median age 65 y; tumor size 5.4 cm). Tumor complexity was high (median RENAL 9, PADUA 10), with a median of three renal arteries (range 1–7). A clampless approach was used in 12 (50%), including five with tumor-specific segmental artery ligation. Ten (42%) underwent total and two (8%) selective clamping (median ischemia 23 min). Median operative time was 240 min, blood loss 500 ml. Two (8.3%) had Clavien ≥ III complications; no conversions occurred. Median eGFR variation at last follow-up (21 mo) was –5.0 ml/min/1.73 m2. Two (8.3%) had positive margins, with no recurrences. Trifecta was achieved in 50%. CONCLUSIONS: 3D-assisted RAPN combining preoperative planning and intraoperative guidance enables precise vascular assessment and individualized ischemia management, improving safety in HSK tumor surgery. These findings support integrating 3D reconstruction into the management of complex renal fusion anomalies.

title: IP05-14: Sutureless Purely Off-Clamp Robotic Partial Nephrectomy: evidence from a randomized controlled non-inferiority trial
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: to describe the novel sutureless (SL) purely off-clamp robotic partial nephrectomy (ocRPN) and compare its results with renorrhaphy (RR). METHODS: a continuous series of patients with cT1-2N0M0 renal tumors, randomly assigned to SL or RR ocRPN, within a single-center, single surgeon randomized controlled trial (GR-2021-12373396). A standard three-arm transperitoneal ocRPN was performed; hemostasis relied on monopolar coagulation of the resection bed. RR was used in controls. Surgical, functional, and oncologic outcomes were collected. Trifecta achievement at discharge tested the non-inferiority hypothesis. Descriptive statistics analyzed the data; recurrence-free survival (RFS) probabilities were compared between groups with the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: among 247 enrolled patients, baseline characteristics were balanced across groups ( Tab. 1). Median operative time was 65 vs 70 minutes in the SL and RR groups (p=0.77). Trifecta was achieved in 93% and 95% of cases, respectively (p=0.43), confirming non-inferiority ( Tab. 2). Blood transfusions (2% vs 0%) and Acute Kidney Injury (2% each) were rare. Nine urinary fistulae occurred overall (3 perioperative, 6 within 90 days), all successfully managed with temporary stenting; rates were higher in the SL group, but not statistically significant. Renal function, assessed by creatinine and scintigraphy, was comparable CONCLUSIONS: SL-ocRPN is safe and effective, representing a feasible alternative to RR-ocRPN in selected cT1-2 renal tumors. Longer follow-up will assess long-term efficacy; further research should clarify which patients benefit more from one technique. | | | --- | | | | | | --- | | |

title: IP05-15: A sutureless Solution: Prospective Comparative Study between a novel haemostatic Patch and Renorrhaphy in Off-Clamp Robot-Assisted Partial Nephrectomy (RAPN)
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I

speakers.organization: IRCCS Bonino Pulejo Piemonte Hospital, Messina

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Renorrhaphy during off-clamp robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) is technically challenging and may potentially impair renal function in the immediate postoperative period. This study evaluates the use of a novel haemostatic patch as an alternative to conventional renorrhaphy in off clamp RAPN. METHODS: From January 2023 to September 2025, we prospectively collected data on patients who underwent off-clamp RAPN at our institution, dividing them into two groups: those who received a patch (Veriset™ Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) on the tumor bed (PG), and those who underwent conventional single-layer renorrhaphy (RG). We compared the two cohorts based on age, body mass index (BMI), tumor laterality and R. E. N. A. L. nephrometry score (NS). Continuous variables were summarized using mean/SD and median/IQR depending on the normal distribution. Paired eGFR (preoperative, postoperative, and 30-day) was analyzed within groups using paired t-test or Wilcoxon test. Between-group differences in ΔHb, eGFR at different time points, console time, enucleation time, and haemostasis time were assessed using independent-sample t-test or Mann-Whitney test. Correlations between ΔHb and clinical/time variables were calculated within each group (Pearson/Spearman). A significance level was set at p<0.05. RESULTS: Table 1 shows the characteristics of the two groups. 24 patients underwent a sutureless approach while 32 underwent a renorraphy approach. Although the PG and the RG differ in age, BMI and tumor laterality (all p<0.05), the mean NS was not statistically significant (p=0.197). In detail, PG had demonstrated significantly reduced console time (p<0.001) and haemostasis time (p=0.013), compared to RG. Additionally, the PG had a higher postoperative day 1 eGFR compared to the RG (p=0.0031). Enucleation time, postoperative ΔHb, Clavien-Dindo complications, length of stay, renal function at 30 days were similar between the two groups. A single patient in the RG required a blood transfusion, while no readmissions for complications occurred. CONCLUSIONS: According to our first experience the application of a haemostatic patch in off-clamp RAPN provided decreased console and hemostasis times, as well as a quicker recovery of renal function compared to traditional renorrhaphy, demonstrating non-inferiority in terms of efficacy and safety. | | | --- | | |

title: IP05-16: Comprehensive Analysis of Delayed Bleeding (DB) Following Partial Nephrectomy (PN)
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I

speakers.organization: Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: DB is an uncommon but potentially serious complication of PN, with a reported incidence of 1-2%. Management options include selective arterial angioembolization (SAE), radical nephrectomy (RN), or conservative management (CM). Our objective was to rigorously identify and characterize the presentation, management, and outcomes of DB in a large cohort of PN patients. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all patients who underwent PN at our institution (2009-2024). Patients with clinical characteristics suggesting hemorrhage and/or post-operative abdominal imaging within 1 month of surgery were screened for possible DB. Patient characteristics and outcomes were collected, and a control group of non-bleed PN patients was included for comparison. RESULTS: 4677 patients underwent PN; 108 (2.3%) experienced DB, and data were also available for 4285 controls (no DB). Median RENAL for patients with DB was only 6 (IQR 5-9)( Table 1). Median time to bleed after PN was 9 days, and the most common presenting symptoms were flank pain (55%) and hematuria (45%). SAE was performed in 64 (59%) patients with a success rate of 92%; 5 (7.8%) required RN. CM was initially pursued in 41 (38%) patients, and 9 (22%) required delayed SAE. Overall, 31 patients (29%) required ICU admission, and the median transfusion requirement was 2 units (IQR 0-3). Three post-DB patients (2.7%) required long-term dialysis. There was no mortality associated with DB. There was no difference in ipsilateral GFR preserved between SAE and CM management ( Table 2), but median global GFR was reduced in DB patients (80%) compared to controls (85%, p=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: In this large cohort, DB after PN was more common than previously reported, likely because past studies have generally excluded CM patients. Fifty percent of DB patients had RENAL≤6, suggesting that even less complex PN cases can be at risk. SAE was successful in >90% of cases and did not further impact functional preservation beyond that observed with CM. CM can also be considered for the management of DB after PN in select patients. Although DB carries substantial risk, encouraging outcomes can be experienced in the great majority of cases. | | | --- | | | | | | --- | | |

title: IP05-17: Perioperative Complications of Low Anterior Access Single Port Retroperitoneal Robotic Partial Nephrectomy versus Multi Port Robotic Partial Nephrectomy
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate and compare the incidence of perioperative complications between Single Port (SP) Low Anterior Access (LAA) Retroperitoneal Robotic Partial Nephrectomy (RAPN) and Multi-Port (MP) RAPN. METHODS: A retrospective review was completed on the prospectively maintained, IRB-approved database of the SP Advanced Research Consortium (SPARC) to identify 458 consecutive patients who underwent LAA Retroperitoneal SP-RAPN between 2022 and 2025. This cohort was compared with MP-RAPN cases performed between 2010 and 2025. Baseline clinicodemographic, intraoperative, and postoperative outcomes were collected, with inferential statistics as presented. Postoperative complications were reported according to the Clavien-Dindo classifications, with major complications defined as those of grade 33a. A multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify the independent predictors of major complications based on age, BMI, comorbidity burden, baseline renal function, tumor complexity, and the robotic surgical approach. RESULTS: A total of 9984 patients were included in our analysis. Compared to MP-RAPN, the SP group was older (median age, 62 vs. 61 years, p=0.037), had a higher BMI (median, 28.8 vs. 27.1 kg/m2, p<0.001), greater comorbidity burden (median CCI, 3 vs. 3, p=0.011), and overall lower tumor complexity (median RENAL score, 6 vs. 7, p<0.001). Intraoperative complications occurred in 2% of the SP-RAPN and 2.9% of the MP-RAPN (p=0.105), while postoperative complications were reported in 12.9% and 12.6% following the SP and MP procedures, respectively (p=0.905). Major complications were similarly low between the two robotic approaches (3.5% vs. 3.1%, p=0.722). On multivariate analysis, the SP approach was not revealed as an independent predictor of major complications (OR 1.730, 95%CI 0.917 – 3.003, p=0.068). However, higher CCI (OR 1.125, 95% CI 1.023 – 1.226, p=0.009), lower preoperative renal function (OR 0.992, 95% CI 1.028 – 1.226, p=0.045), and a higher RENAL score (OR 1.260, 95% CI 1.160 – 1.340, p<0.001) emerged as independent predictors of major postoperative complications. CONCLUSIONS: This multi-institutional comparative study demonstrates that the novel LAA Retroperitoneal SP-RAPN is associated with low perioperative morbidity comparable to MP-RAPN. The favorable complication profile supports its safe integration into the minimally invasive surgical armamentarium for renal tumors.

title: IP05-18: Incidence of Incisional Hernia and Abdominal Wall Bulge Following Low Anterior Access Single Port Robotic Retroperitoneal Partial Nephrectomy: A Report from the Single Port Advanced Research Consortium (SPARC)
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the incidence of incisional hernia and postoperative bulge following Low Anterior Access (LAA) Single Port (SP) Robotic Retroperitoneal Partial Nephrectomy (RAPN) METHODS: A retrospective review was performed on the prospectively maintained, IRB-approved multi-institutional database of the Single Port Advanced Research Consortium (SPARC) to identify 458 consecutive patients who underwent LAA Retroperitoneal SP-RAPN between 2023 and 2025. Postoperative bulge was defined as any protrusion secondary to weakness of the anterior abdominal wall muscle in the absence of any radiological evidence of incisional hernia. Baseline clinicodemographic, perioperative outcomes, and follow-up information were collected, with descriptive statistics as presented. RESULTS: All procedures were completed successfully via a 3-4 cm incision without any evidence of intraoperative complications. At a median follow-up of 12 months (IQR 5.7-20), two patients (0.4%) developed incisional hernia, both of which contained fat and were managed conservatively. Postoperative bulge was reported in six (1.3%) patients, with none requiring additional intervention. When considering some of the risk factors for incisional hernia, the median BMI of our cohort was 29 kg/m2 (IQR 25.1 – 33.2), with 198 (43.2%) reporting active or prior smoking history and 227 (49.6%) reporting prior abdominal surgery. Of the latter, 47 (20.7%) had a history of anterior abdominal wall hernia repair. CONCLUSIONS: LAA Retroperitoneal SP-RAPN can be safely performed with a relatively low risk of postoperative incisional hernia and anterior abdominal wall bulge at a medium-term follow-up.

title: IP05-19: Robotic Partial Nephrectomy in Large Renal Mass: Comparison of Surgical Outcomes Between Patients with cT1 and =cT2 Renal Tumors
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To compare the perioperative, oncological, and renal function outcomes of robotic partial nephrectomy (RAPN) between patients with cT1 and ≥cT2 renal masses. METHODS: A retrospective review was performed on the IRB-approved multi-institutional database of our single institution to identify all consecutive patients who underwent RAPN between 2015 – 2024. Patients were categorized based on their respective tumor size into those greater (≥cT2) or less than 7 cm (cT1). Baseline clinicodemographic, perioperative, and postoperative oncological and renal function outcomes were collected, with inferential statistics as presented. Trifecta outcomes were defined as warm ischemia time (WIT) <25 minutes, negative surgical margins, and absence of postoperative complications. Pentafecta required the achievement of trifecta outcomes, with the addition of >90% renal function preservation and no kidney disease progression at 12 months. RESULTS: Among 2001 patients, 343 (17.1%) cases were identified as ≥cT2. Of these, 57 (16.6%) and 286 (83.4%) had cT2 and cT3 diseases, respectively. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable, although hilar tumors were more prevalent in the ≥cT2 cohort (34.6% vs. 10.2%, p<0.001). Compared with cT1 tumors, ≥cT2 cases demonstrated longer operative time (median, 212 vs. 180 minutes, p<0.001), longer WIT (median, 26 vs. 20 minutes, p<0.001), greater intraoperative blood loss (median, 200 vs. 150 ml, p<0.001), and a higher incidence of major complications (8.5% vs. 3.8%, p<0.001). Positive surgical margin rates remained similar between the groups (8% vs. 5.9%, p=0.146). Trifecta was achieved in 42.3% of the ≥cT2 and 64.7% of the cT1 patients (p<0.001). At 12 months, freedom from kidney disease progression was comparable (80% vs. 81.2%, p=0.615), translating to pentafecta attainment in 19.3% and 31.6% of the respective cohorts (p=0.003). After a median follow-up of 27 months, recurrence rates remained similarly low (3.6% vs. 2%, p=0.089). CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the surgical efficacy of RAPN for large (≥cT2) renal masses, providing similar oncological and renal function outcomes to patients with cT1 tumors, albeit with the increased surgical complexity and morbidity risk. | | | --- | | |

title: IP05-20: Positive Surgical Margins After Partial Nephrectomy: Still a Real Concern or a Fading Threat?
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The prognostic significance of positive surgical margins (PSM) after partial nephrectomy (PN) remains controversial, as most evidence originates from historical cohorts treated with older surgical techniques, limiting its relevance in the era of minimally invasive and robotic approaches. We aimed to reassess their prognostic value in terms of relapse-free survival (RFS), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) within a large and contemporary cohort. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,471 patients who underwent PN between 2000 and 2023 at a tertiary referral center. Patients were stratified according to margin status (PSM vs. negative surgical margins, NSM). Kaplan-Meier analyses estimated RFS, PFS, and OS, while uni- and multivariable Cox regression models tested the association between PSM and local relapse, progression, and all-cause mortality, after adjusting for key covariates including age, smoking habits, comorbidities, tumor stage, and histology. RESULTS: Of 1,471 included patients, 83 (5.6%) had PSM on final pathology. The majority underwent open PN (66%), followed by robot-assisted (24%) and laparoscopic (10%) procedures. Apart from a higher proportion of females in the PSM group (42% vs. 30%, p=0.02), no relevant clinical or pathological differences were observed between groups. At 8-year follow-up, RFS, PFS, and OS were 74% vs. 95% (p=0.001), 88% vs. 92% (p=0.67), and 86% vs. 91% (p=0.19) for PSM vs. NSM, respectively. On MVA, PSM independently predicted a higher risk of local relapse (HR 4.26, p<0.001), but were not associated with disease progression (HR 1.34, p=0.6) or all-cause mortality (HR 2.03, p=0.08). Remarkably, when the analysis was restricted to patients who underwent laparoscopic or robot-assisted PN (n=494), PSM were not significantly associated with local relapse (HR 2.45, p=0.3). CONCLUSIONS: In this large, contemporary series of patients treated with PN, PSM were linked to an increased risk of local recurrence, yet did not significantly affect disease progression or overall survival. These findings suggest that, although PSM should not be underestimated, their long-term prognostic relevance appears limited in the current surgical era—supporting a tailored, surveillance-based approach rather than overtreatment in selected patients.

title: IP05-21: Long-Term Oncological and Functional Outcomes of Robotic Partial Nephrectomy Beyond 10 Years
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the long-term oncological and renal function outcomes of robotic partial nephrectomy (RAPN) in patients with at least ten years of follow-up. METHODS: A retrospective review was completed on the IRB-approved database to identify 2,023 consecutive patients who underwent RAPN between 2015 and 2025. Only patients with at least ten years of follow-up were included. Exclusion criteria were procedures on solitary or horseshoe kidneys, renal transplant recipients, and cases associated with familial syndromes, such as Birt-Hogg-Dubé, Tuberous Sclerosis, and Von-Hippel-Lindau. RESULTS: A total of 260 patients were analyzed, with a median follow-up of 135.6 months (IQR 123 – 147.1 months). The overall survival and recurrence-free survival in our cohort were 90.4% and 97.7%, respectively. At ten years, 65.6% remained free of clinically significant kidney disease progression, with a median renal function preservation of 83.8% (IQR 70.4% – 98.6%). On multivariate analyses, independent predictors of all-cause mortality included advanced age (OR 1.156; 95% CI 1.082 – 1.250, p<0.001), lower preoperative hemoglobin (OR 0.624; 95% CI 0.405 – 0.920, p=0.023), and a higher complexity tumor according to the RENAL score (OR 1.603; 95% CI 1.183 – 2.246, p=0.004). In addition, the predictors of kidney disease progression at ten years were higher comorbidity burden per the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (OR 1.620; 95% CI 1.115 – 2.570, p=0.022), lower preoperative renal function (OR 0.949; 95% CI 0.917 – 0.977, p<0.001), and reduced GFR preservation at one year post-surgery (OR 0.206; 95% CI 0.043 – 0.549, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: RAPN confers relatively favorable long-term oncological and renal function preservation in patients who survive beyond ten years. However, overall survival and risk of kidney disease progression remain influenced by various clinicodemographic and perioperative factors, including age, comorbidity burden, renal function, and tumor complexity.

title: IP05-22: Parenchymal Volume and Functional Recovery after Clamped Partial Nephrectomy (PN): Potential Discrepancies
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I

speakers.organization: Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine

fulltext: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Split renal function (SRF) measurements have enabled evaluation of functional outcomes specific to the kidney exposed to ischemia after PN. Parenchymal volume analysis (PVA) using semiautomated 3D imaging software appears superior to traditional nuclear renal scans (NRS) for assessing SRF. Our objective was to evaluate how ischemia during PN impacts the accuracy of PVA for estimating functional outcomes. METHODS: Retrospective study of all PN (2010-22) at our institution with available pre/postoperative NRS and cross-sectional imaging. Differences between NRS and PVA-derived ipsilateral SRF estimates were evaluated in warm/cold ischemia subgroups. The relationship between ischemia time and PVA/NRS discordance was evaluated with linear and segmented-regression analysis. Correction for PVA overestimation was applied to a previously published cohort of PN patients with prolonged ischemia. RESULTS: Among 437 PN, 246 (56%) and 191 (44%) were managed with warm/cold ischemia, with median ischemia times of 21/28 min, respectively. Preoperative PVA and NRS-based ipsilateral SRF estimates were nearly identical(r=0.94). Post-PN, median PVA-based estimates of ipsilateral SRF were significantly higher than NRS-derived estimates after warm-ischemia(WI)(44% vs. 42%, p=0.001), which was not observed with hypothermia. Segmented regression revealed increasing PVA/NRS discordance at >25 min WI (p=0.04). No relationship was observed between ischemia time and PVA/NRS discordance for hypothermia or limited WI. Correcting for PVA overestimation in an independent cohort demonstrated that functional decline associated with prolonged WI was 2-3-fold greater than estimated by PVA alone. CONCLUSIONS: With prolonged WI, there is discordance between parenchymal volume and function that progressively increases beyond 25 min. Applying this correction to an independent cohort of prolonged WI patients showed a 9% fall in recovery for every 10 min beyond 25 min, 2-fold greater than previously reported for PVA-based estimates. Avoidance of prolonged WI should be considered in patients with solitary kidneys and/or significant pre-existing CKD.

title: IP05-23: Failure-to-Rescue and Age: Lessons from Partial Nephrectomy Patients
parentSessionTitle: IP05: Kidney Cancer: Localized: Surgical Therapy I
