fulltext:
#IP36-28: Increased frequency of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in muscle-
                                                                  invasive bladder cancer after the introduction of adjuvant immunotherapy

                                                                  Satoshi Inoue , Koki Kobayashi , Hiroki Abe , Takanao Omi , Mikinori Kobayashi , Yoko Sugihara , Yuri
                                                                               1                2            3             4                    5               6

                                                                  Yuguchi7, Motohiro Maeda8, KosukeTochigi9, Shusuke Akamatsu1
                                                                  1Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine, Nagoya, Japan, 2Gifu Prefectural Tajimi Hospital, 3Narita Memorial Hospital, 4Toyohashi

                                                                  Municipal Hospital, 5Japanese Red Cross Aichi Medical Center Nagoya Daiichi Hospital, 6Ichinomiya Municipal Hospital, 7Komaki City Hospital,
                                                                  8Chukyo Hospital, 9Yokkaichi Municipal Hospital




 INTRODUCTION                                                              RESULTS
 Nivolumab was approved in Japan on March 2022, as an adjuvant
 immunotherapy (AI) for MIBC.
 Disease-free survival (DFS) improved with adjuvant nivolumab in
 patients with high-risk muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) in
 the CheckMate 274 trial.
 A sub-analysis of the CheckMate 274 trial revealed the possibility of
 a larger effect size in patients treated with neoadjuvant
 chemotherapy (NAC) than in those who had not received NAC.
 Patient selection for perioperative therapy may change over time as
 new clinical evidence emerges.
 We investigated trends in the use of perioperative therapy in
 patients with MIBC.


 METHODS




DISCUSSION
In the post-AI era, patients could choose not only cisplatin-based chemotherapy but also adjuvant nivolumab as
perioperative therapy. Therefore, physicians have increasingly begun to actively selected NAC and adjuvant nivolumab
for MIBC patients to improve treatment outcomes.
For some time after adjuvant nivolumab therapy was approved in Japan, its use in patients who had not received NAC
was generally avoided. Some patients received G-Carbo as NAC with the expectation that they would subsequently
receive adjuvant nivolumab therapy.


CONCLUSIONS
The introduction of AI led to the increased use of NAC and adjuvant therapy in patients with MIBC in real-world practice.
Because of the infrequent use of NAC in patients with renal insufficiency, a regimen indicated for patients with renal
insufficiency is needed.

                                                                                                                                             DISCLOSURES I have no COI with regard to our presentation.

title: IP38-20: Temporal changes in prostate-specific antigen doubling time and their predictive value for second novel androgen receptor signaling inhibitor response in non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer

speakers.organization: Hirosaki University Graduate School of Medicine

fulltext:
Temporal changes in prostate-specific antigen doubling time and their predictive value
for second novel androgen receptor signaling inhibitor response in non-metastatic
castration-resistant prostate cancer                                                                                                                                                        IP38-20
 N. Fujita1, S. Kato2, Y. Kawashima2, M. Shinohara2, R. Tabata3, F. Yoneyama1, S. Sato2, and S. Hatakeyama1                           *Corresponding author’s E-mail address: naonao707012@hirosaki-u.ac.jp
 Department of Urology, 1) Hirosaki University Graduate School of Medicine, Hirosaki, Japan; 2) Ageo Central General Hospital, Ageo, Japan; 3) Sano Kosei General Hospital, Sano, Japan

Background
  Cross-resistance among novel androgen receptor signaling inhibitors (ARSIs) compromises the efficacy of subsequent ARSI treatments.
  Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) doubling time (PSADT) reflects disease status and predicts PSA response to prostate cancer therapies. However, PSADT varies over time, reflecting the current aggressiveness
  of the disease.
  Therefore, we hypothesized that PSADT measured immediately before initiation of a second ARSI may more accurately predict PSA response than PSADT measured at the time of non-metastatic castration-
  resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC) diagnosis.

Methods
 This multicenter retrospective study evaluated 75 patients with nmCRPC who had progressed after treatment with one ARSI and were subsequently treated with a second ARSI.
  The changes in PSADT from diagnosis of nmCRPC to initiation of treatment with a second ARSI were evaluated.
  Moreover, the association between PSA non-responsiveness to treatment with second ARSI and PSADT immediately before initiation of treatment with a second ARSI were evaluated.
  Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors that were significantly associated with PSA non-responsiveness to treatment with a second ARSI.

Results
  The median age at initiation of treatment with a second ARSI was 79 years.
  PSADT measured before the diagnosis of nmCRPC was significantly and positively correlated with that measured immediately before initiation of the second ARSI (Fig. D).
  There was no significant difference in PSADT between the time of nmCRPC diagnosis and the initiation of second ARSI treatment (Fig. E; median 3.6 vs. 4.3 months).
  Among the 75 patients, 31 (41%) experienced some degree of PSADT shortening during treatment with the first ARSI.
  The median change in PSADT from nmCRPC diagnosis to initiation of the second ARSI was 0.6 months (interquartile range: -1.9 to 2.5 months), which was not statistically significant (Fig. F).
  After adjusting for confounding variables, only PSADT immediately before initiation of the second ARSI was significantly and independently associated with PSA non-responsiveness to that treatment (Table).

                                          Belgrade Center for Urogenital Reconstructive Surgery, Belgrade, Serbia


INTRODUCTION                                         RESULTS
Buccal mucosa is now widely regarded as the
preferred graft material for substitution
urethroplasty. However, its limited availability
can pose challenges when reconstructing
extensive or panurethral strictures. We analyzed
our experience using a combination of buccal
mucosa and longitudinal dorsal skin flap for long
anterior urethral strictures.




METHODS                                              CONCLUSIONS
                                                     In this cohort, single-stage reconstruction using a combination of buccal mucosa and genital skin flap
                                                     demonstrated consistent reliability and durability for treating extensive anterior urethral strictures.




A well-vascularized longitudinal dorsal island
skin flap is harvested, transposed ventrally using
a button-hole maneuver and anastomosed to a
buccal mucosa graft. Abundant pedicle of the
flap covers the suture lines.

                                              Bursa Hospital, Bursa, Türkiye, 7Tekirdag Namik Kemal University School of Medicine, Tekirdağ, Türkiye




OBJECTIVE                                                       RESULTS
This study aimed to evaluate the impact of prior clean          The median age of the pre-matched cohort was 61 years (IQR: 43–69), and the median follow-up duration was 11
intermittent catheterization (CIC) on urethral stricture        months (IQR: 8–16). A total of 177 patients (59 with recurrence, 118 without) were analyzed after matching (Table 1).
recurrence following oral mucosal graft urethroplasty           The rate of prior CIC was 11.9% in the recurrence group and 5.1% in the non-recurrence group, with no statistically
(OMGU).                                                         significant difference between the groups (p=0.185). At 12 and 24 months, recurrence-free survival was 69.8% and
                                                                55.8% in patients without prior CIC, compared to 32.4% and 16.2% in those with prior CIC, respectively. Kaplan–Meier
                                                                curves demonstrated significantly lower recurrence-free survival inpatients with a history of CIC (p=0.045).




METHODS
This multicenter retrospective study was conducted
under the Reconstructive Urology, Minimally Invasive
and “Hands-On Training” Working Group of the Turkish
Continence Society. Medical records of 627 patients who
underwent urethroplasty were reviewed. Patients were
excluded if they had missing follow-up data, incomplete
clinical information, underwent urethroplasty other than
oral mucosal graft substitution, or had a history of
previous urethroplasty, pelvic radiotherapy, hypospadias
repair, or lichen sclerosis. After applying these criteria,
228 patients with at least six months of follow-up were
included in the pre-matching cohort. Propensity score
matching (1:2 nearest-neighbor method, caliper 0.1) was
used to minimize baseline differences in age, diabetes,
coronary      artery   disease,    tobacco    use,    prior
catheterization or instrumentation, stricture location and
length, urethroplasty type, number of prior endoscopic
interventions, and time since last intervention.
Recurrence was defined as the detection of a urethral
stricture by cystoscopic and/or radiological evaluation in
symptomatic patients. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis
was performed to compare recurrence-free survival               CONCLUSIONS
according to CIC history.
                                                                Prior CIC is associated with an increased risk of urethral stricture recurrence following OMGU. These findings suggest
                                                                that a history of CIC should be considered during preoperative planning and patient counseling.

Introduction & Objectives
The role of cytoreductive nephrectomy (CN) in metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) remains controversial in the era of modern systemic therapy. We aimed to evaluate the proportion of patients undergoing deferred CN (dCN) and their oncological outcomes in a real-world
multicenter cohort.
Methods
We retrospectively reviewed 651 patients with mRCC who received first-line tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) or immune-oncology (IO) combinations (nivolumab–ipilimumab or IO–TKI) between 2006 and 2025 at 22 Japanese institutions. Patients with prior nephrectomy or follow-up <3
months were excluded, leaving 331 eligible patients (TKI 108, IO–TKI 155, Nivo–Ipi 68). Patients were categorized into dCN and non-nephrectomy groups. The primary endpoint was the proportion of dCN. Secondary endpoints were disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS),
and perioperative outcomes. Multivariable Cox regression with inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied.
Results
Among 331 patients, 58 (17.5%) underwent dCN after a median of 6.6 months of systemic therapy. dCN was associated with longer survival (DFS: HR 0.53; OS: HR 0.31; both p<0.005). Notably, 58.6% of patients achieved favorable outcomes, and 34.5% were able to discontinue
systemic therapy without recurrence, suggesting the possibility of a “functional cure” in a subset. Limitations include retrospective design, modest sample size, and potential selection bias despite adjustment.
Conclusions
dCN was feasible in contemporary real-world practice and may offer survival benefit in selected mRCC patients. Prospective trials are warranted to confirm its role and to refine patient selection.

METHODS
We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing
radical cystectomy for muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma between 2005
and 2025 (n=733), from which those with variant histology (≥10% of the tumor),
identified on transurethral resection or cystectomy specimens, were included.
Patients were stratified according to receipt of guideline-concordant
neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
Clinicopathologic variables were extracted from electronic records. Endpoints
included pathologic complete response (pT0), nodal status (pN0), margin
status, and survival outcomes: overall survival (OS), cancer-specific survival
(CSS), and recurrence-free survival (RFS). Prespecified subgroup analyses
were performed for squamous, micropapillary, and glandular variants.

Introductions and Objectives:                                                                                                                                Materials and Methods:
• In general, pathological T0 is considered to be a good surrogate endpoint in patients with bladder cancer who underwent radical surgery.                   • A total of 1,383 patients with bladder cancer who underwent radical surgery between 2003 and 2024 were retrospectively reviewed using the Michinoku
• However, its incidence and impact on survival outcomes remains largely unknown.                                                                              Japan Urological Cancer Study Group database.
• This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics and survival outcomes in patients with bladder cancer who achieved pT0 or yield                  • Patient data were collected from medical records.
  pT0 following radical surgery.                                                                                                                             • Pathological and survival outcomes were statistically analyzed using the log-rank test, logistic regression analysis, and the Cox proportional hazards model.

Results:                                                                                                                                                     Figure1. Kaplan-Meyer Curve of (A) Extraurotherial Recurrence Free Survival and (B) Overall Survival
• The mean age was 68.6 years, and 1071 (77.6%) patients were male. A total of 865 patients(62.6%) received neoadjuvant chemotherapy
  (NAC), and 248 (28.7%) of them achieved ypT0. In contrast, 64 patients (12.4%) achieved pT0 without neoadjuvant chemotherapy (Table 1).
• Extraurothelial recurrence-free survival was similar between the pT0 and ypT0 groups and was significantly better than that in the non-
  pT0/ypT0 group. The 5-year RFS rates were 86.9%, 89.8% and 59.9%, respectively (p < 0.001) (Figure 1A).
• Overall survival showed a similar trend to recurrence-free survival, no significant difference was observed between the pT0 and ypT0
  groups; however, both showed significantly better outcomes than the non-pT0/ypT0 group (Figure 1B).
• In the multivariable analysis, clinical T stage ≤2 was an independent factor associated with achieving pT0 (OR 4.579, p = 0.002) (Table 2A).
• Clinical T stage ≤2 (OR 2.692, p < 0.001), an eGFR of ≥60 (OR 1.551, p = 0.018), and cisplatin-based NAC (OR 1.697, p = 0.003) were
  independent factors associated with achieving ypT0 (Table 2B).
• In the univariable Cox proportional hazards analysis, ECOG performance status ≥2 was associated with worse RFS after pT0 (HR 23.525, p
  = 0.010) (Table 3A), whereas hydronephrosis before treatment (HR 3.981, p = 0.004) and histological subtype (HR 3.110, p =0.014) were
  associated with worse RFS after ypT0 (Table 3B).

      Conclusions & Future Directions
      Conclusions: Men who learned they had a high-risk prostate cancer PRS were significantly more likely to undergo PSA screening and received more frequent testing over two years compared to average-risk men. This provides

      personalizing cancer screening strategies beyond age-based guidelines, with potential implications for improving early detection in high-risk populations.

                                          Introduction & Objective                                                                               Figure 1. Annual Specialty-Specific Visit Rates by Treatment Group
  •   Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most prevalent non-skin malignancy among U.S. men, with over 3.5 million survivors and 97%
      relative survival at 15 years for localized disease.
  •   Definitive treatments produce distinct toxicity profiles that evolve over a decade or more, requiring specialty-appropriate
      follow-up well beyond the initial post-treatment period.
  •   Guidelines recommend prostate-specific antigen (PSA) surveillance every 6-12 months for 5 years and annually thereafter,
      yet none specifies which specialty should lead long-term follow-up or when care should transition between providers.
  •   Earlier detection of biochemical recurrence at lower PSA levels is associated with improved salvage therapy and survival.
  •   Objective: Describe specialty-specific follow-up patterns over 20 years after definitive treatment for non-metastatic PCa using
      linked SEER-Medicare data.



                                                           Methods
  •   Design: Retrospective linked SEER-Medicare cohort study.
  •   Population: N = 165,276 men aged ≥66 years with non-metastatic PCa treated with definitive therapy (2000-2019).
          • Radical prostatectomy (RP): n = 51,543
          • Radiation therapy (RT: external beam radiation therapy (EBRT) and/or brachytherapy (BT): n = 107,482
          • RP + adjuvant EBRT: n = 6,251
  •   Outcome: Post-treatment Evaluation & Management (E&M) encounters, classified by CMS provider specialty code into
      urology (code 34), radiation oncology (code 92), and medical/hematology oncology (codes 83, 90).
  •   Follow-up: Censored at death, loss of fee-for-service enrollment, retreatment, subsequent pelvic malignancy, chemotherapy,
      late androgen deprivation therapy (ADT, >36 months), or end of study (December 31, 2019).
  •   Analysis: Annual visit rates w/95% CIs; negative-binomial interaction models (years 1-15) quantifying specialty trajectory
      divergence with cluster-robust standard errors; multivariable logistic, Poisson, and Cox models for predictors of oncology
      follow-up in the RT cohort.

title: IP47-20: Therapeutic MMAE Triggers Nectin-4/PD-L1–Positive Exosome Release: Implications for an Adaptive Resistance Pathway to Enfortumab-Vedotin plus Pembrolizumab Therapy

fulltext:
IP47-20                                                                                                                             Therapeutic MMAE Triggers Nectin-4/PD-L1–Positive Exosome
                                                                                                                                     Release: Implications for an Adaptive Resistance Pathway to
                                                                                                                                          Enfortumab-Vedotin plus Pembrolizumab Therapy
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Emma Ushchak1,2, Brendan J. Guercio3,4, Bradley N. Mills4,5, Yi-Fen Lee1,2,4
                                                                                                                        Department of Urology, University of Rochester, NY, USA1 Department of Pathology & Laboratory Medicine, University of Rochester, NY,
                                                                                                                        USA2 Department of Medicine, Hematology/Oncology, University of Rochester, NY, USA3 Wilmot Cancer Center, University of Rochester,
                                                                                                                        NY, USA.4 Department of Surgery, Research, University of Rochester, NY, USA5


•
                                                 BACKGROUND
        Combination of Enfortumab Vedotin (EV), an antibody-drug conjugate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 SUMMARY
        targeting Nectin-4 with a monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE payload), and
        the PD-1 monoclonal antibody pembrolizumab (Pembro) has transformed
        the management of locally advanced and metastatic urothelial carcinoma,
        significantly improving outcomes(1).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           & FUTURE
•       Despite nearly doubling progression free survival, the underlying
        mechanisms driving the development of resistance to EV + Pembro
        remain unclear.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           DIRECTIONS
•       Extracellular vesicles (exosomes) are membrane bound nano-particles                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Urine captures
        released by all nucleated cells, that carry bioactive cargo and offer a                                                                                                                                                               Correlate treatment                                                                                                                                                                                 local disease
        minimally invasive means of monitoring tumor and cellular states in real                                                                                                                                                              outcomes and toxicity                                                                                                                                                                               signals, plasma
        time. They also mediate intercellular communication within the tumor                                                                                                                                                                  with exosome kinetics                                                                                                                                                                               captures systemic
        microenvironment and have been implicated in mediating therapeutic                                                                                                                                                                    and molecular profiles                                                                                                                                                                              and toxicity signals
        resistance, including through exosomal PD-L1, which may promote T cell
        exhaustion and sequester anti-PD-L1 therapeutic antibodies (2).
•       Since EV targets Nectin-4, a protein trafficked through the endocytic and
        vesicular pathways, it is hypothesized that the release of PD-L1+
        and/or Nectin-4+ exosomes may contribute to resistance to EV +
        Pembro therapy.                                                                                                                                                                                METHODS

treatment for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer is transurethral resection of bladder tumors

title: IP48-04: Comparison of SIRS criteria and qSOFA score for predicting severe acute kidney injury development and mortality in febrile urinary tract infection

fulltext:
Comparison of SIRS criteria and qSOFA score for predicting severe acute kidney injury                                                                                                             IP48-04
 development and mortality in febrile urinary tract infection
N. Fujita1,*, M. Momota1, H. Horiguchi1, D. Noro1, O. Soma1, H. Ito2, K. Yoshikawa3, and S. Hatakeyama1                                          *Corresponding author’s E-mail address: naonao707012@hirosaki-u.ac.jp
Department of Urology, 1) Hirosaki University Graduate School of Medicine, Hirosaki, Japan; 2) Aomori Rosai Hospital, Hachinohe, Japan; 3) Aomori City Hospital, Aomori, Japan
Background
  Both the systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) criteria and the quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) score are widely used as screening tools for sepsis.
  Febrile urinary tract infection (UTI), a common cause of sepsis, can lead to serious complications such as acute kidney injury (AKI), which significantly worsens prognosis. Early identification of patients at risk
  for severe AKI and mortality is therefore critical for timely intervention.
  However, previous studies comparing the diagnostic performance of SIRS and qSOFA have yielded conflicting results, and their utility in the context of febrile UTI remains unclear.

Methods                                                                                                                                                                                                                 KDIGO criteria
  This retrospective study included 207 patients with febrile UTI who were treated between March 2017 and March 2019.
  The SIRS criteria and qSOFA score at admission were assessed. AKI was defined according to the KDIGO criteria.
  Total SIRS and qSOFA scores were compared between patients who developed severe AKI and those who did not, as well as between patients who died within 28
  days and those who survived.
  Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate the associations of these scores with severe AKI and 28-day mortality.

Conclusion
 In patients with febrile UTI, the qSOFA score was significantly associated with both the development of severe AKI and short-
 term mortality, whereas the SIRS criteria were not. These findings suggest that the qSOFA score may serve as a more reliable
 and clinically useful prognostic tool than the SIRS criteria in this setting. Incorporating qSOFA into initial assessment protocols
 may help identify high-risk patients earlier and guide timely therapeutic interventions to improve outcomes.

                                                                                                                           antimicrobial stewardship in NHS pre-operative settings.

                                                                                                                                               LIMITATIONS
                                                                                                                           A limitation of Lodestar Dx is that it does not provide
                                                                                                                           antimicrobial susceptibility data.
                                                                                                                           Identifying the specific uropathogen rapidly enables clinicians
                                                                                                                           to apply regional resistance patterns and antibiograms to
                                                                                                                           facilitate the selection of the correct antibiotic, ensuring
                                                                                                                           targeted and effective therapy from the outset.

  dosing regimens
• Aim: prospective evaluation of double-dose MV140 in
  patients with NB

                                                                                                  Median annual infection frequency decreased from 5 to 2 episodes per patient.

    and pre/post infection severity and microbiology.

Elucidation of the mechanism underlying the functional loss of an epigenetic factor, KDM6A, in prostate cancer development
                                        Nobuhito Muramoto1, Masayuki Iwasaki1, Yasuyuki Sera1, Tsuyoshi Fukushima2, Shoichiro Mukai3, Yasutaka Yamada4, Shinichi Sakamoto4, Hisamitsu Ide5, Shigeo Horie5, Hiroaki Honda1
  1Human Disease Models, Institute of Laboratory Animals, Tokyo women's medical university, Tokyo, Japan, 2Section of Oncopathology and Regenerative Biology, Department of Pathology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Miyazaki, Miyazaki, Japan, 3Department of
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                # IP49-04
        Urology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Miyazaki, Miyazaki, Japan, 4Department of Urology, Graduate School of Medicine, University of Chiba, Chiba, Japan, 5Department of Urology, Graduate School of Medicine, Juntendo university, Tokyo, Japan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Abstract
Introduction and Objective: Histone modifications are important for tissue homeostasis, and their mutations are involved in carcinogenesis. Mutations in an X chromosome-specific histone modifier, KDM6A, are common in prostate cancer (PCa), which is frequently associated with loss of its counterpart KDM6C on the
Y chromosome. However, understanding of mechanisms and development of effective treatment for KDM6A-deficient PCa remain elusive. We aimed to address these issues by generating genetically-engineered mice. Methods: We generated prostate-specific Kdm6a-deficient (Kdm6aΔ) mice and crossed them with
Kdm6c knockout mice (Kdm6cΔ) to create mice lacking both Kdm6a and Kdm6c in the prostate (Kdm6aΔ, Kdm6cΔ). To promote tumorigenesis, p53 heterozygosity (p53+/−) was introduced into the mice, and to induce inflammation, mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD). For a therapeutic approach, mice PCa RM-2 cells,
which do not express KDM6C, were genetically engineered to lack KDM6A using the CRISPR-Cas9 system. The Kdm6a-deficient and control RM-2 cells were subcutaneously implanted to generate a syngeneic tumor model. Results: We found that only HFD-treated Kdm6aΔ, Kdm6cΔ, p53+/− mice, not other genotypes
of mice developed progressive PCa. By performing RNA sequencing and pathway analyses using prostate tissues, we found that loss of KDM6A activated inflammatory pathways and concurrently suppressed DNA damage repair pathways. Indeed, immunostaining with F4/80, a macrophage marker, and with γH2AX, a
DNA repair marker, revealed significant macrophage accumulation and prolonged DNA damage repair, respectively, in prostates lacking Kdm6a. Furthermore, in subcutaneous syngeneic models, combined treatment with clodronate liposome (bisphosphonate, a macrophage inhibitor), and olaparib (PARP inhibitor)
efficiently suppressed tumor growth of Kdm6a-deficient RM-2 cells but showed no effect on tumors of control RM-2 cells. Conclusions: These results indicate that loss of KDM6A contributes to PCa development through promoting inflammation and impairing DNA damage repair. Importantly, combined clodronate and
olaparib treatment may serve as a therapeutic strategy for PCa patients with KDM6A mutations.

 INTRODUCTION                                                 RESULTS
 Disease risk-associated plasma proteins are considered       Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 multi-ancestry males, we
 as potential targets in the prevention and treatment of      identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression in mouse models promoted tumor growth, with
 cancers. Elucidating the molecular mechanisms by             transcriptomic profiling revealing activation of cholesterol metabolism and AR signaling, alongside immunosuppression.
 which novel protein drug targets promote the                 Single-cell RNA sequencing of human prostate tumors demonstrated CREB3L4 enrichment in tumor epithelial cells.
 progression of prostate cancer (PCa) and their impact        Interaction analysis indicated that CREB3L4+ tumor cells exhibited enhanced GDF signaling compared to CREB3L4-
 on the immunosuppressive microenvironment can                cells, with CD8+ T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand-receptor analysis and co-culture experiments identified GDF15
 provide interpretably theoretical supplementation            as the key mediator, demonstrating that CREB3L4+ tumor cells suppress CD8+ T cell proliferation and activation through
 thereby aiding in strategies for PCa immunotherapy.          GDF15-TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, prostate-specific knockout or adenovirus-mediated knockdown of CREB3L4
                                                              suppressed tumor growth and was associated with restored CD8+ T cell function, effects that were attenuated by GDF15
                                                              neutralization. Analyses of clinical samples confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, with both
                                                              markers showing inverse correlations with CD8+ T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response.
 METHODS
 Based on multi-cohort plasma proteomic and PCa
 population genomic datasets, the risk protein for the
 development and progression of PCa were identified,
 and the mechanisms of carcinogenesis were explored at
 the transcriptomic level. The impact on devitalized
 CD8+T cells within PCa was excavated at the single-cell
 precision. Using transgenic mice, adenoviruses, and tet-
 on systems, the efficacy of targeted therapy in PCa was
 verified.


CONCLUSIONS
Collectively, these findings reveal a previously
uncharacterized immunomodulatory role of CREB3L4:
CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15
expression, leading to CD8⁺ T cell dysfunction, and thus
warrants further investigation of this pathway as a
candidate therapeutic strategy for PCa.

Purpose:
Resistance to PARP inhibitors (PARPi) remains a major challenge in the
treatment of advanced prostate cancer. While metabolic rewiring has been
implicated in therapy resistance, the molecular drivers and vulnerabilities
underlying this adaptation are not well defined.
Experimental Design:

mitochondrial regulators of PARPi resistance. RNA sequencing and gene set
enrichment analysis (GSEA) were used to profile resistant cell lines, while

activity assays, and immunofluorescence imaging. NDUFS4 was targeted both
genetically with siRNA and pharmacologically with a niclosamide analog,
ARVib-7. Ferroptosis was assessed using FerroOrange staining and analysis
of ferroptosis-associated biomarkers. Clinical relevance was examined using
patient datasets from TCGA and SU2C/PCF cohorts.

title: IP50-02: Oncological benefits of a single immediate instillation of chemotherapy in patients with high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer who receive adjuvant induction bacillus Calmette-Guérin therapy

speakers.organization: Hirosaki University Graduate School of Medicine

fulltext:
Oncological benefits of a single immediate instillation of chemotherapy in patients with high-risk non-
muscle-invasive bladder cancer who receive adjuvant induction bacillus Calmette-Guérin therapy
 N. Fujita1, T. Narita1, M. Momota1, H. Ito2, K. Yoshikawa3, and S. Hatakeyama1                                *Corresponding author’s E-mail address: naonao707012@hirosaki-u.ac.jp
 Department of Urology, 1) Hirosaki University Graduate School of Medicine, Hirosaki, Japan; 2) Aomori Rosai Hospital, Hachinohe, Japan 3) Aomori City Hospital, Aomori, Japan                 IP50-02
Background
  Several studies reported that patients with high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) who received a single immediate instillation of chemotherapy plus induction bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG)
  therapy tended to have better oncological outcomes than those who received induction BCG therapy alone.
  However, due to limited evidence, the clinical utility of a single immediate instillation of chemotherapy following adjuvant induction BCG remains unclear.
Methods
 This retrospective study included 205 patients with high-risk NMIBC who received adjuvant induction BCG therapy after transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT).
  Patients were divided into two groups: those who received a single instillation of chemotherapy plus subsequent adjuvant induction BCG therapy (combined therapy group), and those who received adjuvant
  induction BCG therapy alone (BCG monotherapy group).
  Multivariable analyses using the inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) method to emulate a propensity score-matched population were performed to evaluate the impact of a single instillation of
  chemotherapy on intravesical recurrence-free survival (RFS) and muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC)-free survival.
Results
  Among the 205 patients, 130 (63%) and 75 (37%) were classified as the combined therapy and BCG monotherapy groups, respectively.
  No significant differences in the incidences of perioperative complications of any grade and grade 3 or higher were observed between both groups (Fig. A).
  No significant differences in the BCG therapy discontinuation rate and incidences of overall, local, and systemic adverse events associated with BCG therapy were observed between both groups (Fig. B and C).
  Patients in the combined therapy group had significantly longer intravesical RFS and MIBC-free survival than those in the BCG monotherapy group (Fig. E and F). Multivariable analyses showed that a single
  instillation of chemotherapy was significantly associated with longer intravesical RFS (P < 0.001, hazard ratio [HR]: 0.279; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.150–0.519) and MIBC-free survival (P < 0.001, HR:
  0.078, 95% CI: 0.019–0.317).

                                                       on Testicular Viability after Torsion
                                                       Authors: Silva P., Severo L., Cunha J., Caceiro R., Lança M., Almeida R., Gouveia S., Campos
                                                       Pinheiro L.
                                                       ULS S José; Nova Medical School                                              Lisbon, Portugal



INTRODUCTION                                                                            RESULTS
Testicular torsion represents a time-critical urological emergency, with testicular     A total of 37 patients (aged 21–28 years) were included.
viability directly dependent on prompt diagnosis and surgical intervention. Delays      • Delay before medical consultation: mean 27.7 hours (median 18 h).
at any stage—patient presentation, diagnostic evaluation, or referral—can result        • Delayed presentation (>6 h): 89% of cases (33/37).
in irreversible ischemia and orchiectomy. This study aimed to evaluate the impact       • Diagnostic interval: mean 1.89 hours, longer in peripheral hospitals.
of healthcare access patterns, diagnostic timelines, and demographic variables          • Initial evaluation site: peripheral hospitals 27/37 (73%), tertiary center 10/37 (27%).
on testicular viability in patients treated for torsion at a tertiary center.           • Diagnostic error rate: 8% (3/37). Foreign patients: 16/37 (43%), with significantly longer pre-
                                                                                           hospital delays than nationals.
                                                                                        • Predictor of non-viability: consultation delay >6 hours was the strongest factor associated with
METHODS                                                                                    orchiectomy (p < 0.05).

A retrospective review was performed of all patients who underwent orchiectomy          No significant association was found between diagnostic error and testicular loss once presentation
for testicular torsion between 2017 and 2024. Extracted variables included:             time was accounted for.
• Time intervals: symptom onset to initial medical consultation, and time to
   diagnosis/intervention.
• Healthcare pathway: location of first evaluation (tertiary vs peripheral hospital),   CONCLUSIONS
   presence of misdiagnosis, and referral delays.
• Demographics: age, nationality (national vs foreign), and healthcare access           Delayed presentation remains the dominant predictor of testicular non-viability following torsion,
   characteristics.                                                                     eclipsing diagnostic or institutional factors.
Patients were stratified by these parameters, and associations with testicular non-     Foreign patients experienced longer pre-hospital delays, suggesting barriers in healthcare
viability were analyzed using descriptive and comparative statistics.                   access, awareness, or communication.
                                                                                        Peripheral centers exhibited longer diagnostic intervals, emphasizing the need for standardized
                                                                                        emergency protocols, triage training, and improved ultrasound availability.
                                                                                        Efforts to streamline referral pathways and increase public awareness—particularly among at-risk
                                                                                        populations—are critical to enhancing testicular salvage rates and reducing preventable
                                                                                        orchiectomies.

                                                                  PFUA exposure was independently associated with higher testosterone (β = 0.088; 95% CI 0.032–0.14; p = 0.004), corresponding to a
                                                                  9% increase per log-unit PFUA. Other PFAS showed no significant associations. The PFUA finding persisted across sensitivity models
                                                                  including BMI and metabolic covariates.



                                                                  CONCLUSIONS
                                                                  Contrary to traditional endocrine-disruption paradigms and animal models demonstrating PFUA-mediated Leydig cell inhibition, PFUA
                                                                  exposure was linked to elevated testosterone in U.S. men. This discordance may reflect non-monotonic dose-response effects,
                                                                  compensatory Leydig cell steroidogenesis or species-specific differences. Meta-analytic evidence consistently shows negative
                                                                  associations between other PFAS congeners (PFNA, PFOA) and testosterone, underscoring chain-length–specific endocrine effects.
                                                                  Future longitudinal studies incorporating SHBG, free testosterone and gonadotropin data are needed to clarify PFUA's potentially
                                                                  androgenic mechanism.

CONCLUSION
Socioeconomic disparities have been playing and still play a role in the management of advanced UTUC. Our data show discrepancy among
access to adjuvant chemotherapy in patients undergoing surgery for UTUC depending on the socio-economic status as depicted by ADI. In this
context, further efforts should be made in order to guarantee equity in access to care among the general population

Nephroureterectomy with Ileal Cuff for Upper Tract Recurrence After Radical Cystectomy: Oncologic and Survival Outcomes
Il Woo Park, MD1, Min Uk Park1, Bumjin Lim1, In Gab Jeong1, Jungyo Suh1, Bumsik Hong, MD, PhD1*
1Department of Urology, Asan Medical Center, University of Ulsan College of Medicine, Seoul, Republic of Korea · *Corresponding author: bshong@amc.seoul.kr




   BACKGROUND & AIM                                                                                                                                                                                                                       SURGICAL TECHNIQUE
   Metachronous upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) after radical cystectomy (RC) is uncommon (0.75–6.4%) but represents an aggressive form of panurothelial disease.
   Standard nephroureterectomy (NUX) requires complete excision of the distal ureter and bladder cuff. In post-cystectomy patients this principle extends to the ureteroileal anastomosis
   (the “ileal cuff”).
   However, dense adhesions from the prior cystectomy frequently make complete cuff resection technically demanding, sometimes leading to incomplete resection (cuff failure) — and
   the prognostic impact is unclear.

      Aim: To evaluate whether complete ileal cuff excision affects RFS, CSS, and OS in patients undergoing NUX for UTUC recurrence after RC.

   METHODS
   Single-center retrospective review of a prospectively maintained database (Asan Medical Center; IRB 2025-0349). All patients underwent open NUX for biopsy-proven UTUC recurrence
   after RC.
   Group Definition
   ▸ Cuff (n=18): successful complete cuff excision (operative + pathologic confirmation).
   ▸ Cuff_Fail (n=12): resection aborted intraoperatively due to severe adhesions, difficult access, or risk to adjacent organs.
   Endpoints & Statistics
   ▸ Endpoints: RFS, CSS, OS — measured from NUX.
   ▸ Survival: Kaplan–Meier with log-rank test.
   ▸ Multivariable model: Cox regression with Firth's penalized likelihood to address small-sample bias. Two-sided p < 0.05 considered significant.



   WHY THIS MATTERS
   For traditional NUX, omission of the bladder cuff increases cancer-specific mortality 1.25× in pT3 and 1.45× in pT4 disease (Lughezzani, 2010). Patients undergoing NUX after RC are
   precisely the high-risk population in whom such surgical principles should apply most strictly.
   Yet prior cohort studies of NUX-after-RC have not stratified outcomes by the success of ileal cuff resection — a clinically important knowledge gap that this study addresses.



   IN CONTEXT — PRIOR LITERATURE
   Reported survival in NUX-after-RC cohorts has historically been poor; prior analyses did not stratify by cuff status:
   ▸ Ślusarczyk et al. (2023): 5-yr OS 25.9%
   ▸ Li et al. (2017): 5-yr OS 32%; CSS 35.6%
   Our Cuff_Fail group's 5-yr OS/CSS = 30.6% mirrors these historical cohorts — while the Cuff group reached 5-yr CSS 74.3%.

INTRODUCTION                                                         RESULTS
• Although radical nephroureterectomy with formal
  bladder cuff excision (RNU) is the gold standard for
  the management of upper tract urothelial carcinoma
  (UTUC), evidence supports the use of kidney-sparing
  strategies in appropriately selected patients.

• Accurate diagnosis of UTUC can be challenging and
  concordance between ureteroscopic biopsy (URS Bx)
  and RNU pathology varies.

• We sought to evaluate pathology concordance of
  URS Bx to RNU, considering concomitantly collected
  selective cytologies and the clinical size of tumors on
  imaging.

• In this institutional retrospective review, we identified

26-9272: Genetics-Driven Adaptive Management of Metastatic Clear
                                                    Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma
                                    Authors: Reynier Rodriguez Rosales, Joseph McGrath, Thomas Metzner, Jean-Pierre Kanumuambidi, Arjun
                                            Venkatesh, Yudai Ishiyama, Mohammed Al-Toubat, Hunter Sceats, Mark Bandyk, K.C. Balaji
                                               Department of Urology, University of Florida College of Medicine - Jacksonville

INTRODUCTION                                                                       RESULTS
• Clinical outcomes in metastatic ccRCC remain heterogeneous despite advances
  in immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)– and targeted therapy–based regimens.
• Metastatic progression remains a major determinant of survival, underscoring
  the need for risk stratification strategies.
• Genomic biomarkers have not yet been systematically incorporated into risk-
  adapted surveillance models for metastatic disease.


Objectives: To identify metastasis-enriched genomic alterations that stratify
overall survival, define timing of survival divergence, and reveal potential ICI
response or synthetic-lethal vulnerabilities.


METHODS
• Cohort: 1,395 patients (M1, n=488; M0, n=907) from cBioPortal.
• Genomics: 808 genes analyzed for metastasis enrichment.
• Significant alterations were evaluated for association with OS using Kaplan–
  Meier analysis, log-rank testing, and multi-gene cluster analysis.
• dRMST was used to define the timing of survival divergence.
• Exploratory: ICI response and synthetic-lethality analyses were performed
  using ROC-Plotter and SLOAD.



KEY FINDINGS
                                                                                   CONCLUSIONS
• 8 of 808 profiled genes significantly enriched in metastatic tumors.
                                                                                   • Metastasis-enriched genomic alterations in ccRCC stratified overall survival.
• Improved OS: SETD2, PBRM1, and CDKN2B.
• Adverse OS: PTEN, KDM5C, CDKN2A, and RASA1.                                      • PI3K/cell-cycle–driven alterations were associated with early adverse survival divergence.
• Early survival divergence between 6–18 months (dRMST).                           • Chromatin remodeling alterations showed more favorable survival trajectories.
• ICI response signals: CDKN2A, ALK, and KDM5C as potential                        • Our findings support a novel genomics-guided adaptive management framework for metastatic ccRCC,
  response-associated alterations (AUC range: 0.703–0.725)                           integrating risk stratification with therapeutic decision making.

fulltext:
IP61-23: Improving Safety and Quality of Care in Benign
                                                                        Prostatic Obstruction: A Systematic Review and
                                                                        Network Meta-analysis of Minimally Invasive Treatments
                                                                        Godinho N.J.S., Onofre J.C.M., Colhado C.H., Vilela M.A.D., Menezes T.H.F., Rodrigues H.G., Donalisio R.S.




                                          PURPOSE
Optimizing the management of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) secondary to benign
prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is essential to improving patient safety, efficiency, and quality of care.
However, comprehensive, up-to-date comparative data between contemporary and consolidated
techniques remain scarce. This study aims to directly compare and hierarchically rank the
perioperative safety and early short-term functional outcomes (≤3 months) of the primary surgical
modalities currently available for BPH management.

                                          METHODS
Following PRISMA guidelines, a Bayesian network meta-analysis of RCTs (2015–2025) from
three primary databases was performed to evaluate short-term (≤3 months) functional and safety
outcomes in BPH patients. Interventions were compared individually and by mechanistic class
using a random-effects model, generating 95% credible intervals and SUCRA rankings.
                                                                                                             Figure 1 - PRISMA flow diagram of study screening and selection.
                                           RESULTS
This network meta-analysis of 36 randomized controlled trials (4,782 patients) evaluated 14
interventions. Ablative therapies ranked highest overall for improvements in IPSS and IPSS-QoL
(SUCRA 98.68% and 84.56%, respectively). Enucleation techniques achieved the greatest
reduction in PVR, with ThuLEP leading (SUCRA 95.08%). In contrast, stent/implant therapies and
embolization showed outcomes comparable to sham for PVR reduction. Regarding sexual
function, resection was the only class associated with a significant deterioration in ejaculatory
function compared to sham (MD −3.16; 95% CrI −6.17 to −0.10). Conversely, stent/implant
therapies demonstrated superiority in preserving ejaculatory function (MD −3.20; 95% CrI −5.40 to
−0.90). However, this advantage was not replicated in patient-reported ejaculatory bother, as no
statistically significant differences were observed for this outcome.

                                       CONCLUSION
No intervention was superior to bTURP in urinary efficacy. Stent/Implant approaches showed
significantly inferior urinary outcomes. Although Stent/Implant approaches techniques better
preserved ejaculatory function, this did not reduce patient-reported bother. These findings
underscore the importance of outcome-driven procedure selection, transparent counseling on                   Figure 2 - Postvoidal Resdual Volume: (A) Surface under the cumulative ranking curve
functional trade-offs, and standardized reporting of urinary and sexual endpoints to ensure                  (procedure-specific analysis); (B) forest plot (procedure-specific analysis); (C) surface under the

IP63-24: Global Practices and Perceptions in Stone Burden Assessment: Results
                                          from the International Survey on Stone Volume Measurement

                                                                     Akinbo F1, Pauchard F 1, Larrañaga M2, Salvadó JA1,2
                                1University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center, Case Western Reserve University, School of Medicine
                                                             2Universidad Finis Terrae, Facultad de Medicina, Santiago de Chile




                         INTRODUCTION                                                                                                                     RESULTS

• Preoperative stone burden measurement drives procedure choice,
  access planning, operative time estimates, and outcome reporting.              • 252 urologists from six continents; 91.7% were attending urologists.
• Despite stones being 3D, routine practice and guidelines still rely mainly     • 83% routinely use maximum diameter; only 27% use any volumetric
  on maximum linear diameter.                                                      metric.
• Linear sizing shows meaningful variability and becomes less reliable as        • Among volumetry users, geometric formulas (sphere/ellipsoid) were
  stones get larger or more irregular.                                             most common (62%); 3D segmentation/PACS tools were rare (<10%).
• Geometric volume estimates (sphere/ellipsoid) help but remain                  • Most reported <5 minutes per case for volume; 82% agreed volume
  imprecise compared with CT-based segmentation.                                   better represents stone burden than diameter.
• Semi-automated and AI tools can generate fast, accurate volumes, but           • Volumetry use was higher in <10 years practice (p=0.04) and academic
  real-world adoption and PACS/EHR integration remain limited and                  settings (p<0.05); 87% would adopt if automated tools were available
  poorly quantified.


                             OBJECTIVE
This study aimed to characterize current global practices,
preferences, and perceived barriers related to stone volume
assessment among urologists.

                             METHODS
We conducted an anonymous, web-based cross-sectional survey of
urologists and trainees involved in stone care (September to
November 2025), distributed via the EAU Urolithiasis Section,
Endourological Society, and other professional networks. The
SurveyMonkey questionnaire assessed demographics, primary
preoperative sizing metric (diameter, volume, or both), volumetric
methods used, CT protocol factors, time required per case,
perceived feasibility, attitudes, laser performance metrics, and
open-text barriers, with branching to show CT- and volume-specific                                                                                  CONCLUSIONS
items only when relevant.
The primary outcome was the preferred preoperative stone burden
metric; secondary outcomes included tool use, workflow time,                      • Global survey shows a clear implementation gap between evidence-supported perceptions and routine stone burden measurement
feasibility, and barriers. Responses were summarized as frequencies                practices
and percentages with varying denominators, and compared by
experience (<10 vs ≥10 years), fellowship status, and practice setting            • Although most urologists view volumetric metrics as superior, adoption remains limited by workflow friction and tool accessibility.
using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests (two-sided p<0.05); analyses             • Standardized, automated, rapid volumetric solutions are needed to enable consistent measurement and reporting across institutions.
were performed in R. The study was exempt human subjects
research.

INTRODUCTION
Adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer patients face critical
fertility preservation decisions during a vulnerable time.
Treatment urgency, emotional distress, and financial barriers
create challenges to informed decision-making. Despite ASRM
recommendations for comprehensive fertility preservation
counseling, patients receive inconsistent guidance due to absent
standardized protocols and specialty variability. This study
compares sperm cryopreservation counseling by Reproductive
Endocrinology and Infertility (REI) specialists and urologists for
AYA cancer patients.


METHODS




                                                                                                 CONCLUSIONS
                                                                                                 Urologists were more responsive to social and financial
                                                                                                 factors—partnership status, mortality risk, insurance
                                                                                                 coverage, and orchiectomy—while REI specialists
                                                                                                 maintained more standardized approaches. Patients may
                                                                                                 receive substantially different fertility preservation guidance
                                                                                                 depending on the specialist consulted, highlighting the need
                                                                                                 for evidence-based, standardized counseling protocols for
                                                                                                 AYA cancer patients.

Non-Robotic    Radical Prostatectomy

MarvinKevin D. Li, Marvin
       N. Carlisle,       N. Li,

                                                                                                                                  Faris, BenjaminBenjamin N. Breyer
                                                                                                                                                   N. Breyer



                           Introduction & Objective                                                                      Figure 1: Cumulative Incidence of Any UAE
 • Urinary adverse events (UAEs) after radical prostatectomy (RP) drive
   significant morbidity and reinterventions.
 • Comparative data for robot-assisted (RARP) vs. non-robotic (non-RARP) in
   older men, particularly in the mature robotic era, remain limited.
 • Widespread RARP adoption necessitates clearer understanding of long-term
   functional outcome profiles compared to non-RARP approaches.
 • Objective: compare RARP vs. non-RARP postoperative cumulative incidence
   and adjusted hazards of UAEs and related procedures.



                                           Methods
 • Design: Retrospective SEER-Medicare (2010-2018) cohort study.
 • Population: 17,441 Medicare beneficiaries (≥66 yrs) with localized prostate
   cancer treated with RP.
 • Groups:
   • RARP:    14,769 (84.7%)
   • Non-RARP: 2,672 (15.3%)
 • Outcome: Any postoperative UAE (defined by prespecified codes), UAE
                                                                                                                  Figure 2: Adjusted Hazard Ratios for Specific UAEs
   subtypes, and subsequent urethral/bladder procedures.
 • Analysis: Cumulative incidence (Kaplan-Meier) and multivariable Cox
   proportional hazards models, adjusting for age, race, income, year, tumor
   stage/grade, baseline UAE, and Charlson comorbidity.



                                             Results
 • Primary Outcome: RARP was associated with a 50% reduction in the
   hazard of any postoperative UAE.
    • Overall Rate: 7.7% (RARP) vs. 15.3% (Non-RARP)
    • aHR: 0.50 (95% CI 0.45-0.57), p<0.001
 • Driving Factor: This RARP benefit was driven by a ~70-80% reduction in
   Bladder Outlet Obstruction (BOO) and related procedures.
    • BOO diagnosis: aHR 0.27
    • Bladder Neck Incision: aHR 0.20
 • Non-Factor: No differences in incontinence rates or subsequent procedures.
    • Incontinence Diagnosis: aHR 0.97 (95% CI 0.75-1.26)




                                        Conclusions
 • In this large, contemporary Medicare beneficiary cohort, RARP displayed half
   the hazard of experiencing any UAE compared to non-RARP approaches.
 • This benefit is driven by a dramatic reduction in BOO and related                                                                                    Key Takeaway
   interventions, not by different incontinence incidence.                                                     • RARP is associated with half the risk of any UAE (aHR 0.50).
 • These population-level data inform patient counseling and quality                                           • Large reductions in Bladder Outlet Obstruction (aHR 0.27) drive this benefit.
   benchmarking in older men, highlighting a key advantage of robotic
   approaches in the mature surgical era.                                                                      • No difference was found in incontinence rates (aHR 0.97).

INTRODUCTION                                                           RESULTS
Germline genetic testing (GGT) is recommended for patients             A total of 3614 pts with RCC and 6985 cancer-unaffected pts were included.
(pts) with renal cell carcinoma (RCC) and bilateral/multifocal         In the RCC cohort, 50% were female and mean age at testing was 55 years.
disease, specific variant histology, a diagnosis < 46 years old, or    In the cancer-free cohort, 84% were female and the mean age at testing was 66.
a family history of renal neoplastic syndrome. Retrospective           The PGV prevalence was 8.7% in the RCC cohort and 8.9% in the cancer-unaffected
studies of selected cohorts with advanced disease or                   cohort. Multivariable analysis of any PGVs were similar in the RCC vs cancer-
suggestive personal/family histories show a pathogenic/likely          unaffected cohorts (OR 0.93; 95% CI 0.79-1.10). However, PGVs in RCC
pathogenic germline variant (PGV) prevalence of 5-18%.                 predisposition genes were enriched in the RCC cohort vs cancer-unaffected cohort
However, the prevalence of PGVs and clinical utility of GGT in         (OR 2.73; 95% CI 1.91-3.92) and PGVs in DDR genes were reduced in the RCC cohort
unselected cohorts of pts with RCC remains largely unknown.            vs cancer-unaffected cohort (OR 0.68; 95% CI 0.55-0.83).



METHODS
All pts with an ICD-10 diagnosis code of RCC who underwent
hereditary cancer multi-gene panel testing (MGPT) through
Ambry Genetics from 2019-2021 were identified; clinician-
reported clinical history was abstracted for those with PGVs.
A cancer-unaffected cohort of pts who underwent MGPT during
the same timeframe was also identified, excluding those
younger than 60 years old. This analysis focused on PGVs in 67
genes, including 13 RCC predisposition genes, 20 DNA damage
repair (DDR) genes, and 34 other genes.
Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the
association between PGV status and RCC diagnosis, adjusting
for age at testing, race, and sex at birth.

        CONCLUSIONS
        The overall prevalence of PGVs was approximately 9% in both RCC and cancer-unaffected cohorts. RCC predisposition genes were enriched
        in pts with RCC and DDR genes were enriched in cancer-unaffected pts. These findings support broader implementation of GGT for pts with
        RCC to guide screening for additional malignancies, management in advanced disease, and cascade genetic testing for family members.

fulltext:
IP72-01: Mobile-based Assessment of Entrustable
                                                                                                                                                         Professional Activities in Urology Training:
                                                                                                                                                         Implementation and Outcomes
                                                                                                                                                         Fabian J. Aschwanden1,2, Luca Afferi1,2, Lukas Kandler3, Adrian P. Marty3, Philipp Baumeister¹, Agostino Mattei1,2,
                                                                                                                                                         Marko Kozomara1,2, Christian D. Fankhauser1,2,3
                                                                                                                                                         1 Faculty of Health Sciences and Medicine, University of Lucerne, Lucerne, Switzerland
                                                                                                                                                         2 Clinic for Urology, University Teaching and Research Hospital of the University of Lucerne, Lucerne, Switzerland
                                                                                                                                                         3 University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland




INTRODUCTION                                                                                                                                                 RESULTS & CONCLUSIONS
Competency-based medical education is shifting surgical
training from time- and volume-based progression toward
documented competence in defined clinical activities.
Entrustable professional activities provide a structured
framework for assessing observable units of professional
practice. However, implementation in daily clinical training is
often limited by delayed feedback, inconsistent assessment
criteria, and difficulty tracking residents’ progress over time.
Mobile technology may facilitate real-time workplace-based
assessment by making feedback faster, more frequent, and
easier to document.
Objective: To implement and evaluate a smartphone-based EPA
assessment tool for real-time feedback and competency tracking
in urology residency training.


METHODS
A two-phase implementation project was conducted at a Swiss
urology training institution.
Phase 1:
• A consultant working group defined 46 urology-specific EPAs
   covering general, specialty-specific, preoperative,
   intraoperative, postoperative, emergency, and nonoperative
   technical tasks.
Phase 2:
• The preparedEPA smartphone application was introduced into
   routine clinical training. The app was installed by 13 trainees
   and 10 supervisors.
• After completing an EPA under supervision, the trainee initiated
   an assessment in the app. Both trainee and supervisor
   independently rated task complexity and the required level of
   future supervision using a five-level entrustment-supervision
   scale: observe, direct supervision, indirect supervision, distant
   supervision, and supervise others.
• Assessment characteristics were analyzed descriptively.
   Agreement between trainees and supervisors was evaluated
   using weighted Cohen’s κ and Fleiss’ κ.
DISCLOSURES
This work was supported by a 2023 Gilead SAKK Expanding Horizons in Oncology Award to Christian D. Fankhauser.
Adrian P. Marty and Lukas Kandler serve on the board of directors at PrecisionED Ltd., the company developing the preparedEPA application.
Generative AI was used to support the visual structuring and graphical preparation of this poster; all scientific content was reviewed and verified by
the authors.

title: IP73-02: Protective role of bone-modifying agents against febrile neutropenia in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer receiving upfront docetaxel
parentSessionTitle: IP73: Prostate Cancer: Advanced (including drug therapy) III

speakers.organization: Hirosaki University Graduate School of Medicine, Japan

fulltext:
Protective role of bone-modifying agents against febrile neutropenia
                         in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer receiving
                         upfront docetaxel
                         S. Tazawa¹, N. Fujita¹, F. Yoneyama¹, T. Ichiyama¹, S. Hosogoe¹, K. Togashi¹, H. Asanuma¹, H. Horiguchi¹, Y. Ishibashi¹, W. Fukuokaya²,
                         T. Yanagisawa², S. Narita³, T. Kimura², T. Habuchi³, S. Hatakeyama¹                                                                        I have no COI to
   IP73-02               1) Hirosaki University Graduate School of Medicine, Urology, Hirosaki, Japan ; 2) The Jikei University, School of Medicine, Urology,           disclose.
                         Tokyo, Japan ; 3) Akita University School of Medicine, Urology, Akita, Japan                                                              Shunsuke Tazawa


  Introduction & Objectives
  The introduction of upfront docetaxel, including triplet therapy, has significantly transformed the systemic treatment landscape for metastatic hormone-sensitive
  prostate cancer (mHSPC). However, it can cause severe hematological toxicities, including febrile neutropenia (FN). Given the close relationship between
  neutropenia and bone marrow function, and the role of bone-modifying agents (BMAs) in modulating the bone marrow microenvironment, we hypothesized that
  patients receiving combined therapy with docetaxel and BMAs may have a lower risk of FN compared to those receiving docetaxel alone.
  Materials & Methods
  This retrospective study included 214 patients with mHSPC who received upfront docetaxel, including darolutamide-based triplet therapy, between December
  2015 and September 2025. FN was defined according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0. BMAs included zoledronic acid and
  denosumab. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify risk factors for FN. Additionally, subgroup analyses were conducted to evaluate
  the association between BMA use and FN incidence across clinical subgroups, including age, docetaxel dose, and extent of disease (EOD) score.
  Results
  The median age and docetaxel dose were 71 years and 70 mg/m², respectively. Of the 214 patients, 115 (54%) received BMAs during mHSPC treatment. FN of
  grade 3 or higher occurred in 28 patients (13%). The incidence rate of FN was significantly lower in patients treated with BMAs compared to those who were not
  (Fig. A). In univariable analyses, higher docetaxel dose was significantly associated with increased FN risk, while BMA use was significantly associated with
  reduced risk (Fig. B). In contrast, extent of disease score and primary prophylactic administration of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) were not
  significantly associated with FN. After adjusting for age, only BMA use remained significantly associated with FN. Subgroup analyses revealed that the protective
  effect of BMAs was not observed in patients receiving lower docetaxel doses or those with lower bone metastasis burden.




Conclusion
FN occurred in 13% of patients with mHSPC receiving upfront docetaxel. BMA use may be associated with a reduced risk of FN,
although its benefit may be limited in patients with lower chemotherapy intensity or disease burden.
